Atlas System Audit 11 FRM - First-Come Reward Model Criticality Critical Location LockupFlow.sol#L77 DailyFlow.sol#L76 Status Unresolved Description The contracts pay user rewards by withdrawing from the shared PancakeSwap V3 position instead of using isolated reward reserves. As a result, users are e ff ectively paid from shared deposited liquidity, meaning earlier claimers can consume liquidity that later users rely on. function claim(uint256 orderId) external override nonReentrant() { ... uint256 amount = _withdrawPool(orderInfo.amountEarned, orderInfo.tokenId); ... } function claim(uint256 orderId) external override nonReentrant() { ... (uint256 rewardTotal, uint256 daysAlreadyRewared, uint256 daysMustBeRewared) = _getPendingRewardsAmount(orderInfo); ... uint256 amount = _withdrawPool(rewardTotal, orderInfo.tokenId); ... } Recommendation The team is advised to separate user principal from reward funding and implement explicit reward reserve accounting. This will prevent user payouts from depending on the availability of shared liquidity deposited by other users.

Page 13
Atlas System Audit 12 AOW - Arbitrary Owner Withdrawal Criticality Medium Location Transport.sol#L28 Status Unresolved Description The claimReferral() function allows the owner to withdraw an arbitrary amount of liquidity from the PancakeSwap V3 position without verifying that the amount corresponds to accrued referral rewards. Since the contract does not maintain referral accounting or claim limits, the owner can withdraw any amount from the underlying position, including liquidity that may be required to satisfy user claims in the other protocol fl ows. The impact of this issue is further expanded by the overall protocol design. The protocol includes a Distrib.sol contract, which is intended to distribute referral and partner rewards. Rather than maintaining its own liquidity, Distrib.sol is funded through calls to claimReferral() function claimReferral(address user, uint256 amount) external override onlyOwner { ... uint256 realAmount = _withdrawPool(amount, tokenId); … } Recommendation The team is advised to implement referral accounting, claim limits, and proof of entitlement before allowing withdrawals, as well as a separate funding mechanism for referral and partner rewards that does not rely on liquidity backing user deposits. This will ensure that referral payouts cannot exceed the amounts legitimately owed. Additionally, the team should decouple partner reward distribution from direct withdrawals of the PancakeSwap V3 position by maintaining dedicated accounting for distributable funds.

Page 14
Atlas System Audit 13 CRD - Claims Range Dependent Criticality Medium Location PositionHandler.sol#L126 Status Unresolved Description All claim and withdrawal fl ows require the PancakeSwap V3 position to be fully on the expected side of the pool. As a result, if the current tick is not below tickLower for token0 or not at/above tickUpper for token1, users cannot claim or withdraw even if their order has matured or rewards are available. if (tokenIsToken0) { require(tick < tickLower, "Wrong side"); } else { require(tick >= tickUpper, "Wrong side"); } Recommendation The team is advised to handle cases where positions are outside the range. This will prevent valid claims from being blocked simply because the market price has moved into the LP range.

Page 15
Atlas System Audit 14 CCR - Contract Centralization Risk Criticality Minor / Informative Location Transport.sol LockupFlow.sol DailyFlow.sol Distrib.sol Status Unresolved Description The contract's functionality and behavior are heavily dependent on external parameters or con fi gurations. While external con fi guration can o ff er fl exibility, it also poses several centralization risks that warrant attention. Centralization risks arising from the dependence on external con fi guration include Single Point of Control, Vulnerability to Attacks, Operational Delays, Trust Dependencies, and Decentralization Erosion. function setTreasury(address treasury_) external override onlyOwner { _setTreasury(treasury_); } function setFee(uint256 fee_) external override onlyOwner { _setFee(fee_); } function setTokenId(uint256 tokenId_) external override onlyOwner { _changeTokenId(tokenId_); } Recommendation To address this fi nding and mitigate centralization risks, it is recommended to evaluate the feasibility of migrating critical con fi gurations and functionality into the contract's codebase itself. This approach would reduce external dependencies and enhance the contract's self-su ffi ciency. It is essential to carefully weigh the trade-o ff s between external con fi guration fl exibility and the risks associated with centralization.

Page 16
Atlas System Audit 15 ELFM - Exceeds Fees Limit Criticality Minor / Informative Location Transport.sol#L52,65 LockupFlow.sol#L96,146 Distrib.sol#L56,65 DailyFlow.sol#L136,149 Status Unresolved Description The contract owner has the authority to increase fees over a reasonable allowed limit. The owner may take advantage of it by calling the setFee function with a high percentage value. function setFee(uint256 fee_) external override onlyOwner { _setFee(fee_); } function _setFee(uint256 fee_) internal { require(fee_ <= PRECISION, "Fee too high"); platformFee = fee_; }

Page 17
Atlas System Audit 16 Recommendation The contract could embody a check for the maximum acceptable value. The team should carefully manage the private keys of the owner’s account. We strongly recommend a powerful security mechanism that will prevent a single user from accessing the contract admin functions. Temporary Solutions: These measurements do not decrease the severity of the fi nding ● Introduce a time-locker mechanism with a reasonable delay. ● Introduce a multi-signature wallet so that many addresses will con fi rm the action. ● Introduce a governance model where users will vote about the actions. Permanent Solution: ● Renouncing the ownership, which will eliminate the threats but it is non-reversible.

Page 18
Atlas System Audit 17 IWH - Insu ffi cient Withdrawal Handling Criticality Minor / Informative Location LockupFlow.sol#L66 DailyFlow.sol#L66 Status Unresolved Description The contracts assume that _withdrawPool() returns enough tokens to cover the expected claim amount and fee, but there is no minimum output protection during liquidity withdrawal. As a result, if the withdrawn amount is lower than expected, users may be underpaid, unable to recover the remaining amount, or the claim may revert due to an under fl ow when calculating amount - fee . function claim(uint256 orderId) external override nonReentrant() { ... orderInfo.notClaimed = false; ... uint256 amount = _withdrawPool(orderInfo.amountEarned, orderInfo.tokenId); ... token.safeTransfer(msg.sender, amount - fee); ... } function claim(uint256 orderId) external override nonReentrant() { ... uint256 amount = _withdrawPool(rewardTotal, orderInfo.tokenId); ... token.safeTransfer(msg.sender, amount - fee); orderInfo.lastClaimed = uint64(block.timestamp); orderInfo.amountUnclaimed -= amount; ... }

Page 19
Atlas System Audit 18 Recommendation The team is advised to enforce minimum withdrawal amounts and handle partial withdrawals explicitly. This will prevent unexpected underpayments, avoid under fl ow reverts, and ensure users can still claim any unpaid remaining amount in a later transaction.

Page 20
Atlas System Audit 19 LBR - Liquidity Base Reduction Criticality Minor / Informative Location PositionHandler.sol#L96 Status Unresolved Description The contracts pay claims by removing liquidity from the PancakeSwap V3 position instead of keeping the tokens in the protocol to continue generating LP fees. As a result, every successful claim reduces the active liquidity base and may reduce the protocol’s ability to generate future rewards. function _withdrawPool(uint256 amount, uint256 tokenId_) internal returns (uint256 amountOut) { _checkPositionSide(tokenId_); uint128 liquidity = _getLiquidityForAmount(amount, tokenId_); INonfungiblePositionManager.DecreaseLiquidityParams memory paramsDecrease = INonfungiblePositionManager.DecreaseLiquidityParams({ tokenId: tokenId_, liquidity: liquidity, amount0Min: 0, amount1Min: 0, deadline: block.timestamp }); nfpm.decreaseLiquidity(paramsDecrease); ... } Recommendation The team is advised to evaluate whether rewards should be paid from a separate reserve instead of directly withdrawing LP liquidity. This will help preserve the protocol’s liquidity base and support future fee generation.

Page 21
Atlas System Audit 20 MTC - Manipulatable Tick Check Criticality Minor / Informative Location PositionHandler.sol#L126 Status Unresolved Description The contract uses the pool’s current slot0() tick to determine whether the position is on the correct side, but this value re fl ects the spot price and can be temporarily manipulated through swaps. As a result, actors with su ffi cient capital may in fl uence whether deposits, withdrawals, or claims pass the side check. (, int24 tick,,,,,) = pool.slot0(); Recommendation The team is advised to use a TWAP-based check or another manipulation-resistant price source instead of relying only on the spot tick. This will reduce the impact of temporary price manipulation on protocol operations.

Page 22
Atlas System Audit 21 NOM - NFT Ownership Missing Criticality Minor / Informative Location PositionHandler.sol#L56,82 Status Unresolved Description The contract interacts with PancakeSwap V3 positions through the Nonfungible Position Manager, but it never veri fi es that the contract owns the provided NFT position. As a result, core actions such as increasing liquidity, decreasing liquidity, or collecting tokens may revert if the NFT is held externally. (, uint256 amount0, uint256 amount1) = nfpm.increaseLiquidity(params); nfpm.decreaseLiquidity(paramsDecrease); (uint256 amount0, uint256 amount1) = nfpm.collect(paramsCollect); Recommendation The team is advised to validate that the contract owns the NFT position before using it. This will prevent unexpected reverts and ensure that all liquidity operations can be executed reliably.

Page 23
Atlas System Audit 22 NFU - Non-USDT Fees Unhandled Criticality Minor / Informative Location PositionHandler.sol#L106 Status Unresolved Description The contract collects both tokens from the PancakeSwap V3 position, but the main contracts only account for and transfer the con fi gured token , which appears to be the USDT-side token. As a result, any collected amount of the non-USDT token remains unhandled in the contract and may become stuck or excluded from protocol accounting. (uint256 amount0, uint256 amount1) = nfpm.collect(paramsCollect); amountOut = tokenIsToken0 ? amount0 : amount1; Recommendation The team is advised to explicitly account for both tokens returned by collect() . This will prevent non-USDT fees from being ignored, stuck, or excluded from the intended fee and reward distribution logic.

Page 24
Atlas System Audit 23 NTC - Non-USDT Token Control Criticality Minor / Informative Location PositionHandler.sol#L40 Status Unresolved Description The protocol depends on a PancakeSwap V3 pair that includes a non-USDT token, and if the owner or a trusted party controls that token, they may be able to manipulate the pool price or liquidity economics by minting, dumping, burning, or otherwise controlling supply. As a result, the owner may in fl uence the tick range condition, a ff ect whether users can claim, distort the value of LP liquidity, and increase the amount of USDT or fees extracted from the pool. pool = IPancakeV3Pool(factory.getPool(token0, token1, fee)); Recommendation The team is advised to avoid relying on a pool paired with a centrally controlled or arbitrarily mintable token. This will reduce the risk that privileged control over the non-USDT token can be used to manipulate claims, liquidity value, or protocol accounting.

Page 25
Atlas System Audit 24 PAI - Possible Approval Incompatibility Criticality Minor / Informative Location PositionHandler.sol#L60 Status Unresolved Description The contract uses the standard approve() function to authorize the PancakeSwap Nonfungible Position Manager to spend tokens before increasing liquidity. For weird ERC-20 tokens calls to approve() may revert, preventing future deposits and reducing compatibility with such tokens. token.approve(address(nfpm), amount); Recommendation The team is advised to replace approve() with SafeERC20.forceApprove(). This will ensure compatibility with weird ERC-20 tokens and prevent future deposits from unexpectedly reverting.

Page 26
Atlas System Audit 25 PDFD - Possible Double Fee Deduction Criticality Minor / Informative Location Transport.sol#L40 Distrib.sol#L44 Status Unresolved Description The protocol contains two independent fee mechanisms for referral distributions. Both Transport.claimReferral() and Distrib.distribute() deduct a platformFee before transferring funds to the recipient. If the intended referral fl ow is for Transport to withdraw liquidity from the PancakeSwap V3 position, transfer the funds to Distrib , and for Distrib to distribute them to partners, the same referral payment may be charged a platform fee twice. As a result, recipients may receive less than the intended reward, while the treasury collects fees at two separate stages of the same payout. Although this may be intentional, the current implementation does not document the behavior or prevent accidental double charging. function claimReferral(address user, uint256 amount) external override onlyOwner { ... uint256 fee = (realAmount * platformFee) / PRECISION; token.safeTransfer(treasury, fee + positionRewards); token.safeTransfer(user, realAmount - fee); … }

Page 27
Atlas System Audit 26 function distribute(address user, uint256 amount) external override onlyOwner nonReentrant { ... uint256 fee = (amount * platformFee) / PRECISION; token.safeTransfer(treasury, fee); token.safeTransfer(user, amount - fee); … } Recommendation The team should clearly de fi ne where referral fees are intended to be collected and ensure that each referral payout is charged at most once. If Distrib is responsible for partner distributions, Transport should forward the full referral amount without deducting a fee. Alternatively, if Transport already collects the platform fee, Distrib should distribute the received funds without applying an additional deduction.

Page 28
Atlas System Audit 27 PTAI - Potential Transfer Amount Inconsistency Criticality Minor / Informative Location PositionHandler.sol#L59 Status Unresolved Description The transfer() and transferFrom() functions are used to transfer a speci fi ed amount of tokens to an address. The fee or tax is an amount that is charged to the sender of an ERC20 token when tokens are transferred to another address. According to the speci fi cation, the transferred amount could potentially be less than the expected amount. This may produce inconsistency between the expected and the actual behavior. The following example depicts the diversion between the expected and actual amount. Tax Amount Expected Actual No Tax 100 100 100 10% Tax 100 100 90 function _depositPool(uint256 amount, uint256 tokenId_) internal returns (uint256 amountOut) { ... token.safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amount); ... }

Page 29
Atlas System Audit 28 Recommendation The team is advised to take into consideration the actual amount that has been transferred instead of the expected. It is important to note that an ERC20 transfer tax is not a standard feature of the ERC20 speci fi cation, and it is not universally implemented by all ERC20 contracts. Therefore, the contract could produce the actual amount by calculating the di ff erence between the transfer call. Actual Transferred Amount = Balance After Transfer - Balance Before Transfer

Page 30
Atlas System Audit 29 RLW - Rounded Liquidity Withdrawal Criticality Minor / Informative Location PositionHandler.sol#L123 Status Unresolved Description The contract increases the calculated liquidity by one before withdrawing from the position. As a result, the contract may attempt to burn slightly more liquidity than required, which can cause unexpected reverts due to insu ffi ciency or withdraw more liquidity than intended that will be directed to the treasury address. require(liquidity > 0, "Amount too small"); liquidity += 1; Recommendation The team is advised to avoid blindly increasing the calculated liquidity or to cap the value against the position’s available liquidity. This will prevent over-withdrawal attempts and make the withdrawal behavior more predictable.

Page 31
Atlas System Audit 30 SMC - Strict Maturity Check Criticality Minor / Informative Location LockupFlow.sol#L71 Status Unresolved Description The contract requires the current timestamp to be strictly greater than the order fi nish time before allowing a claim. As a result, users cannot claim exactly at the maturity timestamp and must wait at least one additional second. require(orderInfo.finished < block.timestamp, "Not yet time to claim"); Recommendation The team is advised to use a greater-than-or-equal comparison for this maturity check. This will align the claim condition with the expected meaning of a fi nished lockup period.

Page 32
Atlas System Audit 31 URR - Unrealistic Reward Rates Criticality Minor / Informative Location DailyFlow.sol#L156 LockupFlow.sol#L172 Status Unresolved Description The contracts o ff er fi xed rewards that appear very high compared to the short claim or lockup periods, but there is no guaranteed external revenue source shown that can sustainably fund these payouts. As a result, the reward model may be economically unrealistic unless it is externally funded or consistently supported by su ffi cient LP fees. return 110 * BP; return 130 * BP; else if (tier == ILockupFlow.LockupFlowTier.Launch) { rewards = (amount * (30 * BP)) / PRECISION; } else if (tier == ILockupFlow.LockupFlowTier.Momentum) { rewards = (amount * (200 * BP)) / PRECISION; } else if (tier == ILockupFlow.LockupFlowTier.Premiere) { rewards = (amount * (500 * BP)) / PRECISION; } else if (tier == ILockupFlow.LockupFlowTier.President) { rewards = (amount * (1200 * BP)) / PRECISION; } else if (tier == ILockupFlow.LockupFlowTier.Imperium) { rewards = (amount * (2250 * BP)) / PRECISION; } Recommendation The team is advised to document the reward funding source and ensure the reward rates are backed by realistic revenue assumptions. This will make the protocol’s economic model clearer and reduce the risk of unsustainable promised returns.

Page 33
Atlas System Audit 32 L04 - Conformance to Solidity Naming Conventions Criticality Minor / Informative Location PositionHandler.sol#L17,18 Status Unresolved Description The Solidity style guide is a set of guidelines for writing clean and consistent Solidity code. Adhering to a style guide can help improve the readability and maintainability of the Solidity code, making it easier for others to understand and work with. The followings are a few key points from the Solidity style guide: 1. Use camelCase for function and variable names, with the fi rst letter in lowercase (e.g., myVariable, updateCounter). 2. Use PascalCase for contract, struct, and enum names, with the fi rst letter in uppercase (e.g., MyContract, UserStruct, ErrorEnum). 3. Use uppercase for constant variables and enums (e.g., MAX_VALUE, ERROR_CODE). 4. Use indentation to improve readability and structure. 5. Use spaces between operators and after commas. 6. Use comments to explain the purpose and behavior of the code. 7. Keep lines short (around 120 characters) to improve readability. IPancakeV3Factory constant factory = IPancakeV3Factory(0x0BFbCF9fa4f9C56B0F40a671Ad40E0805A091865) INonfungiblePositionManager constant nfpm = INonfungiblePositionManager(0x46A15B0b27311cedF172AB29E4f4766fbE7F4364 )

Page 34
Atlas System Audit 33 Recommendation By following the Solidity naming convention guidelines, the codebase increased the readability, maintainability, and makes it easier to work with. Find more information on the Solidity documentation https://docs.soliditylang.org/en/stable/style-guide.html#naming-conventions .

Page 35
Atlas System Audit 34 L13 - Divide before Multiply Operation Criticality Minor / Informative Location DailyFlow.sol#L57,187,188 Status Unresolved Description It is important to be aware of the order of operations when performing arithmetic calculations. This is especially important when working with large numbers, as the order of operations can a ff ect the fi nal result of the calculation. Performing divisions before multiplications may cause loss of prediction. orderInfo.amountUnclaimed = ((amount * _getRewardRate(tier)) / PRECISION) * DAILY_REWARDS_COUNT Recommendation To avoid this issue, it is recommended to carefully consider the order of operations when performing arithmetic calculations in Solidity. It's generally a good idea to use parentheses to specify the order of operations. The basic rule is that the multiplications should be prior to the divisions.

Page 36
Atlas System Audit 35 L19 - Stable Compiler Version Criticality Minor / Informative Location PositionHandler.sol#L2 LockupFlow.sol#L2 ITransport.sol#L2 ILockupFlow.sol#L2 IDailyFlow.sol#L2 Status Unresolved Description The ^ symbol indicates that any version of Solidity that is compatible with the speci fi ed version (i.e., any version that is a higher minor or patch version) can be used to compile the contract. The version lock is a mechanism that allows the author to specify a minimum version of the Solidity compiler that must be used to compile the contract code. This is useful because it ensures that the contract will be compiled using a version of the compiler that is known to be compatible with the code. pragma solidity ^0.8.20; Recommendation The team is advised to lock the pragma to ensure the stability of the codebase. The locked pragma version ensures that the contract will not be deployed with an unexpected version. An unexpected version may produce vulnerabilities and undiscovered bugs. The compiler should be con fi gured to the lowest version that provides all the required functionality for the codebase. As a result, the project will be compiled in a well-tested LTS (Long Term Support) environment.

``` atlas Security Audit Page 3 of 17 Summary of Audit Results After auditing , 1 Low-risk were identified in the atlas project. Specific audit details will be presented in the Findings section. Users should pay attention to the following aspects when interacting with this project: Low Fixed : 0 Acknowledged : 1

Page 4
``` atlas Security Audit Page 4 of 17  Project Description: Atlas is a staking and yield-farming project built on PancakeSwap V3 . This audit focuses primarily on the following three business contracts — DailyFlow, LockupFlow, Distrib and Transport — each of which is described in turn below. DailyFlow offers a 200-day staking product that releases rewards linearly on a daily basis. After a user deposits tokens via lockup , the contract automatically assigns the order to one of two tiers (Core or Elite , divided at the 2000 threshold), each carrying a different daily reward rate, and locks in the order's principal, start/end times, and projected total rewards at the moment of creation. The user may subsequently call claim to collect the rewards accrued over the days elapsed; the contract computes the payable amount based on the actual number of calendar days passed (capped at 200 days), deducts the platform fee platformFee , and pays the remainder to the user, while the fee and any surplus yield generated by the liquidity position are funneled to treasury. The contract also exposes query interfaces such as getOrder and getUserOrders , along with administrative functions — controlled by the project team — for adjusting the fee, the treasury account, and the active position. LockupFlow offers a fixed-term product that pays principal plus interest in a single settlement at maturity, complementing the day-by-day release model of DailyFlow . When a user places an order through lockup, they select a lockup tier ( LockupFlowTier , ranging from a 10-minute test tier up to the 30-day Imperium tier across six levels, where longer terms carry higher reward rates); the contract then derives the maturity time from the tier and fixes the principal, earned rewards, and net payout (after fees) in a single step. Funds cannot be withdrawn during the lockup period — only upon maturity may the user claim; at redemption, the contract verifies that the order has not already been claimed (notClaimed) and that it has matured, then settles principal and interest, deducts the fee, and disburses the balance to the user. Transport handles the distribution of the platform's referral/rebate rewards, whose amounts are settled off-chain and then submitted on-chain by the project team for payout. Its core function, claimReferral , is restricted to the contract Owner; the administrator disburses a specified amount to a designated user on their behalf, likewise deducting the platform fee and crediting both the fee and any surplus position yield to treasury. Unlike the other two contracts, Transport maintains no user staking orders or state and serves purely as a funds-disbursement endpoint. All three contracts inherit from PositionHandler and share the deposit/withdraw logic such as _depositPool and _withdrawPool, consolidating business funds into a single-sided (single-token) PancakeV3 liquidity position to achieve centralized custody of funds and aggregation of yield.

Page 5
``` atlas Security Audit Page 5 of 17 Distrib is a token distribution contract: the contract holds an ERC20 token balance (funded by the Transport contract). The owner (backend) calls distribute to pay out tokens to a specified user — at payout, a platform fee is calculated and deducted based on the platformFee rate (with precision PRECISION = 1e25 ), transferred to the treasury, and the remainder is sent to the user.

Page 6
``` atlas Security Audit Page 6 of 17 1 Overview 1.1 Project Overview Project N ame atlas Project L anguage Solidity Platform BNB Chain File Hash(SHA256) 69cac44e294f0fd5a4d17dd7d59685b82b1f7a55050313405212639a8731da54 1.2 Audit Overview Audit work duration: Jun 15 , 202 6 – Jun 17 , 202 6 Audit team: Beosin Security Team 1. 3 Audit Method The audit methods are as follows : 1. Formal Verification Formal verification is a technique that uses property-based approaches for testing and verification. Property specifications define a set of rules using Beosin's library of security expert rules. These rules call into the contracts under analysis and make various assertions about their behavior. The rules of the specification play a crucial role in the analysis. If the rule is violated, a concrete test case is provided to demonstrate the violation. 2. Manual Review Using manual auditing methods, the code is read line by line to identify potential security issues. This ensures that the contract's execution logic aligns with the client's specifications and intentions, thereby safeguarding the accuracy of the contract's business logic. The manual audit is divided into three groups to cover the entire auditing process: The Basic Testing Group is primarily responsible for interpreting the project's code and conducting comprehensive functional testing.

Page 7
``` atlas Security Audit Page 7 of 17 The Simulated Attack Group is responsible for analyzing the audited project based on the collected historical audit vulnerability database and security incident attack models. They identify potential attack vectors and collaborate with the Basic Testing Group to conduct simulated attack tests. The Expert Analysis Group is responsible for analyzing the overall project design, interactions with third parties, and security risks in the on-chain operational environment. They also conduct a review of the entire audit findings. 3. Static Analysis Static analysis is a function of examining code during compilation or static analysis to detect issues. Beosin-VaaS can detect more than 100 common smart contract vulnerabilities through static analysis, such as reentrancy and block parameter dependency. It allows early and efficient discovery of problems to improve code quality and security.

Page 8
``` atlas Security Audit Page 8 of 17 2 Findings Index Risk description Severity level Status atlas-01 Centralization Risk Low Acknowledged

Page 9
``` atlas Security Audit Page 9 of 17 Finding Details: [ atlas-01 ] Centralization Risk Severity Level Low Lines PositionHandler.sol#L26-42 Type Business Security Description All three contracts (Transport, DailyFlow, and LockupFlow) share the same liquidity-position NFT held by the project team. Users generate orders by staking their assets into the contracts, but the underlying position NFT remains under the project team's control and is managed entirely by them. During this period, if a private key is leaked, the owner acts maliciously, or keys are mismanaged, an attacker could manipulate the underlying position through that NFT, thereby posing a centralization risk to users' staked assets. constructor ( address token_ , uint256 tokenId_ ) { require (tokenId_ != 0 , "Invalid token id" ); token = IERC20Metadata (token_); tokenDecimals = token. decimals (); tokenId = tokenId_; Recommendation It is recommended to place the contract owner and its associated privileges under the management of a multisig wallet to eliminate the single point of failure of a single private key. Status Acknowledged . The project team confirmed that this behavior is part of the intended business logic and aligns with the project design.

Page 10
``` atlas Security Audit Page 10 of 17 3 Appendix 3.1 Vulnerability Asses 1 sment Metrics and Status in Smart Contracts 3.1.1 Metrics In order to objectively assess the severity level of vulnerabilities in blockchain systems, this report provides detailed assessment metrics for security vulnerabilities in smart contracts with reference to CVSS 3.1 (Common Vulnerability Scoring System Ver 3.1). According to the severity level of vulnerability, the vulnerabilities are classified into four levels: "critical", "high", "medium" and "low". It mainly relies on the degree of impact and likelihood of exploitation of the vulnerability, supplemented by other comprehensive factors to determine of the severity level. Impact Likelihood Severe High Medium Low Probable Critical High Medium Low Possible High Medium Medium Low Unlikely Medium Medium Low Info Rare Low Low Info Info

Page 11
``` atlas Security Audit Page 11 of 17 3.1.2 Degree of impact  Critical Critical impact generally refers to the vulnerability can have a serious impact on the confidentiality, integrity, availability of smart contracts or their economic model, which can cause substantial economic losses to the contract business system, large-scale data disruption, loss of authority management, failure of key functions, loss of credibility, or indirectly affect the operation of other smart contracts associated with it and cause substantial losses, as well as other severe and mostly irreversible harm.  High High impact generally refers to the vulnerability can have a relatively serious impact on the confidentiality, integrity, availability of the smart contract or its economic model, which can cause a greater economic loss, local functional unavailability, loss of credibility and other impact to the contract business system.  Medium Medium impact generally refers to the vulnerability can have a relatively minor impact on the confidentiality, integrity, availability of the smart contract or its economic model, which can cause a small amount of economic loss to the contract business system, individual business unavailability and other impact.  Low Low impact generally refers to the vulnerability can have a minor impact on the smart contract, which can pose certain security threat to the contract business system and needs to be improved. 3.1. 3 Likelihood of Exploitation  Probable Probable likelihood generally means that the cost required to exploit the vulnerability is low, with no special exploitation threshold, and the vulnerability can be triggered consistently.  Possible Possible likelihood generally means that exploiting such vulnerability requires a certain cost, or there are certain conditions for exploitation, and the vulnerability is not easily and consistently triggered.

Page 12
``` atlas Security Audit Page 12 of 17  Unlikely Unlikely likelihood generally means that the vulnerability requires a high cost, or the exploitation conditions are very demanding and the vulnerability is highly difficult to trigger.  Rare Rare likelihood generally means that the vulnerability requires an extremely high cost or the conditions for exploitation are extremely difficult to achieve. 3.1. 4 Fix Results Status Status Description Fixe d The project party fully fixes a vulnerability. Partially Fixe d The project party did not fully fix the issue, but only mitigated the issue. Acknowledged The project party confirms and chooses to ignore the issue.

Page 13
``` atlas Security Audit Page 13 of 17 3.2 Audit Categories No. Categories Subitems 1 Coding Conventions Compiler Version Security Deprecated Items Redundant Code require/assert Usage Gas Consumption 2 General Vulnerability Integer Overflow/Underflow Reentrancy Pseudo-random Number Generator (PRNG) Transaction-Ordering Dependence DoS (Denial of Service) Function Call Permissions call/delegatecall Security Returned Value Security tx.origin Usage Replay Attack Overriding Variables Third-party Protocol Interface Consistency 3 Business Security Business Logics Business Implementations Manipulable Token Price Centralized Asset Control Asset Tradability Arbitrage Attack Beosin classified the security issues of smart contracts into three categories: Coding Conventions, General Vulnerability, Business Security. Their specific definitions are as follows:  Coding Conventions

Page 14
``` atlas Security Audit Page 14 of 17 Audit whether smart contracts follow recommended language security coding practices. For example, smart contracts developed in Solidity language should fix the compiler version and do not use deprecated keywords.  General Vulnerability General Vulnerability include some common vulnerabilities that may appear in smart contract projects. These vulnerabilities are mainly related to the characteristics of the smart contract itself, such as integer overflow/underflow and denial of service attacks.  Business Security Business security is mainly related to some issues related to the business realized by each project, and has a relatively strong pertinence. For example, whether the lock-up plan in the code match the white paper, or the flash loan attack caused by the incorrect setting of the price acquisition oracle. * Note that the project may suffer stake losses due to the integrated third-party protocol. This is not something Beosin can control. Business security requires the participation of the project party. The project party and users need to stay vigilant at all times.

``` atlas Security Audit Page 15 of 17 3.3 Disclaimer The Audit Report issued by Beosin is related to the services agreed in the relevant service agreement. The Project Party or the Served Party (hereinafter referred to as the "Served Party") can only be used within the conditions and scope agreed in the service agreement. Other third parties shall not transmit, disclose, quote, rely on or tamper with the Audit Report issued for any purpose. The Audit Report issued by Beosin is made solely for the code, and any description, expression or wording contained therein shall not be interpreted as affirmation or confirmation of the project, nor shall any warranty or guarantee be given as to the absolute flawlessness of the code analyzed, the code team, the business model or legal compliance. However, due to the technical limitations of any organization, and in the event that the code provided by the Served Party is missing information, tampered with, deleted, hidden or subsequently altered, the audit report may still fail to fully enumerate all the risks. The Audit Report issued by Beosin in no way provides investment advice on any project, nor should it be utilized as investment suggestions of any type. This report represents an extensive evaluation process designed to help our customers improve code quality while mitigating the high risks in blockchain.

``` atlas Security Audit Page 16 of 17 3.4 About Beosin Beosin is a leading blockchain security and compliance technology company established in 2018. Being focused on blockchain ecosystem security and compliance, it has developed a product matrix including Beosin KYT, Beosin Trace, and Stablecoin Monitor, which have obtained international certifications such as ISO 27001 and SOC 2. Beosin's core products have been applied for over 70 intellectual property rights, and the company has participated in the development of multiple international standards related to blockchain security. It was among the first batch of enterprises selected for the Cyberport Incubation Programme. Atlas Ecosystem

Smart Cycle is the first financial protocol and the core of the Atlas System ecosystem.

It allows participants to join mutual aid cycles, where funds are distributed and all conditions are fulfilled automatically through a smart contract.

Thanks to its open logic, each participant understands the rules of interaction in advance and can track transactions in real time within the blockchain system.

Smart Cycle combines blockchain transparency, process automation, and community support in a single digital environment.

Invite & Earn is Atlas System's referral program: invite others, build your team, and earn rewards based on its activity.

The model is built on a transparent, multi-level system of statuses, personal volume, and team growth. The more actively a participant develops their structure, the more opportunities open up within the referral program.

Invite & Earn helps scale the Atlas System community, unite participants around a unified ecosystem, and maintain long-term relationships between partners and invited teams.

A centralized knowledge base of the Atlas System ecosystem, which contains all the key information about the operation of the platform.

Here participants can find instructions, explanations of protocol mechanisms, and answers to frequently asked questions.

An educational platform for the Atlas System ecosystem, designed to train participants in working with the system and developing financial literacy.

P2P Exchange creates a convenient infrastructure for working with digital assets within the system and simplifies interaction between participants from different countries.

A digital wallet for the Atlas System ecosystem, designed to store funds and interact with the platform’s smart contracts.

With its help, participants can connect to Atlas System protocols, manage their assets and participate in the financial cycles of the system.

Cryptowallet provides secure access to the Atlas System infrastructure and serves as the primary tool for working with digital assets within the ecosystem.

A partner program for specialists in digital marketing and audience acquisition.

It allows advertising and traffic professionals to partner with the Atlas ecosystem and earn rewards for bringing in new users.

The program creates an additional growth channel for the platform and opens up opportunities for partners who work with advertising and digital promotion channels.

A secure messenger for communication between participants of the Atlas System ecosystem.

It is designed for communication within the community, sharing experience, and coordinating teams.

Atlas Talk creates a unified space for user interaction, where participants can discuss the development of the system, share knowledge, and stay in touch with each other.

A decentralized governance system for the Atlas ecosystem.

It allows participants to take part in votes and influence the development of the platform's protocols and future products.

Through the Governance mechanism, the community can propose changes, discuss new solutions, and take part in shaping the future architecture of Atlas System.

A decentralized platform for exchanging digital assets within the Atlas ecosystem.

It makes it possible to swap tokens and other digital assets quickly and securely, without the involvement of centralized services.

Swap DAO supports the liquidity of the ecosystem and creates the infrastructure for working with participants' digital assets.

The financial center of the Atlas System ecosystem, designed to develop new financial instruments and manage system reserves.

Bank DAO forms the basis for the long-term development of the platform and expansion of its financial capabilities.

This module creates the infrastructure to launch new products, allocate resources, and maintain the sustainability of the entire Atlas System ecosystem.

How it works

If your structure includes partners with lower percentage qualifications, you receive the percentage difference between your status and the status of these partners.

If a partner in your structure achieves an equal or higher status, you stop receiving Partner Rewards from their structure, since all Delta is distributed according to their own qualifications.

This is how the rule works: the most active partner earns, not the one at the top. A partner below them can surpass their inviters in status and can receive significantly higher Partner Rewards. The system motivates participants to be active: rewards are not allocated to inactive participants.

Let's say your status is Builder 4 (27%). This means that you have the right to receive 27% of the Delta of the participants in your structure, provided that their percentage qualification is lower than yours.

You personally invited a partner who, in terms of cycle volume and structure, corresponds to the Builder 3 status (24%). This partner, in turn, has a participant in its structure (at any depth), who, at the selected rate, generates Delta of $1,000.

According to the terms of the referral program: a partner with the status of Builder 3 (24%) receives their Partner Reward: 24% of $1,000 = $240. You, as an upline partner with Builder 4 status (27%), receive the difference between the percentage qualifications: 27% – 24% = 3%.

Thus, your Partner Reward will be: 3% of $1,000 = $30.

If your structure did not have a partner with Builder 3 status, you would receive the full Partner Reward according to your qualifications - 27%, that is, $270.

If a lower-level partner reaches Builder 4 (27%) status equal to yours, or reaches a higher status, you stop receiving Partner Rewards from their structure, since he fully realizes his percentage qualification on his own.

Partner Structure Volume Accounting

Actual Partner Structure Volume - the total volume of the structure without applying coefficients

Weighted Partner Structure Volume - the volume taken into account by the system after applying depth coefficients

Accounting for Daily Flow in the structure’s qualifying volume

To calculate partner status, cycle volume is counted based on its duration and its role in the Atlas marketing model:

short-term Smart Cycle plans are counted with a coefficient of 1.0, meaning 100% of the amount;

Daily Flow plans are counted with a coefficient of 0.5, meaning 50% of the created cycle amount.

Example:

an Imperium cycle for 100 USDT adds 100 USDT of qualifying volume;

a Daily Flow cycle for 100 USDT adds 50 USDT of qualifying volume;

1,000 USDT in short-term cycles and 1,000 USDT in Daily Flow create a total qualifying volume of 1,500 USDT.

Formula:

Qualifying volume =
short-term cycle volume × 1.0
+ Daily Flow volume × 0.5

The coefficient is applied only when calculating structure volume and partner status. It does not reduce the Daily Flow amount itself, change the cycle duration, Claim rules, or the calculation procedure for the delta provided by the terms.

Rationale

The Atlas partner model is primarily focused on active community development through short-term cycles. These require more regular participation and better reflect the structure’s current activity.

Daily Flow is designed for a significantly longer period. If counted equally with short-term cycles, a large long-term cycle could result in a disproportionately fast status upgrade without comparable regular activity. This creates a qualification advantage and may disrupt the balance between participants.

The 0.5 coefficient:

preserves Daily Flow’s contribution to qualification;

makes status reflect sustained structure activity;

reduces the possibility of accelerated status upgrades based only on large long-term cycles;

supports balance between different participation formats;

matches the original logic of the marketing model, which is focused on short-term cycles.

More About the Partner Program

Registration in the Partner Program occurs automatically after creating the first Smart Cycle with a Support Amount of $10 or more.

To participate, just invite new users using your referral link. Partner Rewards are calculated automatically according to your Partner Status.

Detailed statistics are available in your personal account: the number of partners, the volume of their activity and the amount of accrued partner rewards.

In your personal account, you see the entire structure of your team: first-line partners and the depth of the built network.

The volume of participant activity, your current status and the amount of accrued Partner Rewards are displayed.

The calculation mechanism is based on pre-established rules of the referral program. All accruals are recorded in the system and are available for verification.

Transactions related to the transfer of funds on the blockchain can be verified through public tools (BSCScan).

From the start, each partner has access to 15% of Delta received personally by the invited participant.

The most active and productive partners can receive up to 60% of Delta generated by lower members of the structure at an unlimited number of levels.

This was made possible by a Partner Program built on a linear, step-by-step marketing model with compression, where the joining date is not the key factor, but the volume of work done and the development of the structure.

Участники могут присоединяться к циклам помощи, отслеживать их выполнение и получать поддержку от сообщества в рамках установленной логики протокола.

Как это работает

Если в вашей структуре находятся партнёры с более низкой процентной квалификацией, вы получаете разницу процентов между вашим статусом и статусом этих партнёров.

Если партнёр в вашей структуре достигает равного или более высокого статуса, вы перестаете получать партнерский доход с его структуры, поскольку вся добавочная помощь (дельта) распределяется согласно его собственной квалификации.

Таким образом работает правило: зарабатывает наиболее активный, а не тот кто стоит наверху. Нижестоящий партнер может обогнать по статусам своих пригласителей и зарабатывать в разы больше бонусов. Система мотивирует участников проявлять активность, деньги не уходят на выплату неактивным участникам системы.

Допустим, ваш статус Builder 4 (27%). Допустим, у вас статус Builder 4 (27%). Это означает, что вы имеете право получать 27% от добавочного помощи (delta) участников вашей структуры, при условии, что их процентная квалификация ниже вашей.

Вы лично пригласили партнёра, который по объёму циклов и структуры соответствует статусу Builder 3 (24%). Этот партнёр, в свою очередь, имеет участника в своей структуре (на любой глубине), который по выбранному тарифу получает добавочную помощь (delta) в размере $1.000.

Согласно условиям партнёрской программы: партнёр со статусом Builder 3 (24%) получает свой бонус: 24% от $1.000 = $240. Вы, как вышестоящий партнёр со статусом Builder 4 (27%), получаете разницу между процентными квалификациями: 27% – 24% = 3%.

Таким образом, ваш партнерский бонус составит: 3% от $1 000 = $30.

Если бы в вашей структуре не было партнёра со статусом Builder 3, вы получили бы полный бонус по своей квалификации — 27%, то есть $270.

В случае, если нижестоящий партнёр достигает статуса Builder 4 (27%), равного вашему, либо выходит на более высокий статус, вы прекращаете получать партнёрский бонус с его структуры, так как он полностью реализует свою процентную квалификацию самостоятельно.

Учет объема партнерской структуры

Фактический объем структуры партнера — общий объем структуры без применения коэффициентов

Зачетный объем партнерской структуры — объем, который система учитывает после применения коэффициентов глубины

Accounting for Daily Flow in the structure’s qualifying volume

To calculate partner status, cycle volume is counted based on its duration and its role in the Atlas marketing model:

short-term Smart Cycle plans are counted with a coefficient of 1.0, meaning 100% of the amount;

Daily Flow plans are counted with a coefficient of 0.5, meaning 50% of the created cycle amount.

Example:

an Imperium cycle for 100 USDT adds 100 USDT of qualifying volume;

a Daily Flow cycle for 100 USDT adds 50 USDT of qualifying volume;

1,000 USDT in short-term cycles and 1,000 USDT in Daily Flow create a total qualifying volume of 1,500 USDT.

Formula:

Qualifying volume =
short-term cycle volume × 1.0
+ Daily Flow volume × 0.5

The coefficient is applied only when calculating structure volume and partner status. It does not reduce the Daily Flow amount itself, change the cycle duration, Claim rules, or the calculation procedure for the delta provided by the terms.

Rationale

The Atlas partner model is primarily focused on active community development through short-term cycles. These require more regular participation and better reflect the structure’s current activity.

Daily Flow is designed for a significantly longer period. If counted equally with short-term cycles, a large long-term cycle could result in a disproportionately fast status upgrade without comparable regular activity. This creates a qualification advantage and may disrupt the balance between participants.

The 0.5 coefficient:

preserves Daily Flow’s contribution to qualification;

makes status reflect sustained structure activity;

reduces the possibility of accelerated status upgrades based only on large long-term cycles;

supports balance between different participation formats;

matches the original logic of the marketing model, which is focused on short-term cycles.

Подробнее о Партнерской программе

Регистрация в партнёрской программе происходит автоматически после создания Smart Cycle 1 на сумму от 10 $.

Для участия достаточно пригласить новых пользователей по своей реферальной ссылке. Начисления по партнёрской программе рассчитываются автоматически в соответствии с вашим статусом.

В личном кабинете доступна подробная статистика: количество партнёров, объём их активности и сумма начисленных партнёрских вознаграждений.

В личном кабинете вы видите всю структуру своей команды: партнёров первой линии и глубину построенной сети.

В личном кабинете отображаются объем активности участников, ваш текущий статус и сумма начисленных партнерских вознаграждений.

Механизм расчёта основан на заранее установленных правилах партнёрской программы. Все начисления фиксируются в системе и доступны для проверки.

Транзакции, связанные с переводом средств в блокчейне, можно проверить через публичные инструменты (BSCScan).

Каждому партнёру со старта доступно 15% от добавочной помощи (delta), полученной лично приглашённым участником.

Наиболее активные и результативные партнеры могут получать до 60% от дельты, сформированной участниками нижних уровней структуры, на неограниченной глубине.

Это стало возможным благодаря партнёрской программе, построенной по модели линейного ступенчатого маркетинга с компрессией, где значение имеет не дата присоединения к платформе, а объём проделанной работы и развитие структуры.

Smart Cycle 2

Smart Cycle 2 — это следующий этап развития механики Smart Cycle в рамках Atlas System.

У каждого Smart Cycle есть свой жизненный путь: он может развиваться, набирать обороты, замедляться и со временем приближаться к завершению. Atlas не скрывает эту цикличность — напротив, она является частью архитектуры системы.

sources.title: atlas audit explanation en
sources.content:
Page 1
1 1. About the document and audit boundaries Cyberscope checked a set of source files PositionHandler.sol , Transport.sol , LockupFlow.sol , DailyFlow.sol , Distrib.sol and related interfaces. The Corrected Phase 2 version of the report contains 20 comments: 1 Critical; 2 Medium; 17 Minor / Informative. OFFICIAL DOCUMENT Explanation Atlas System for Cyberscope audit Report: Cyberscope, Corrected Phase 2 Report date: June 30, 2026 Network: BNB Smart Chain Explanation version: 2.0 Date of explanation: July 25, 2026 This is the official comment Atlas System for each auditor ’ s comment. The document does not refute the audit, change the assigned criticality, or declare comments closed. His task is to translate technical statements into understandable language and explain how the corresponding part of the system is organized in Atlas.

Page 2
All 20 comments are marked by the auditor as Unresolved . This clarification does not change this status. If Atlas describes an actual configuration that reduces the applicability of a particular scenario, this is an explanation of the current configuration, not a standalone closure of the note. The audit refers to specific source files and their SHA-256 listed in the June 30, 2026 report. After this date, the architecture could receive new deployments or changed versions of contracts. In particular, the current address Daily Flow V2 is included in the current register, but should not automatically be considered the audited June report without a separate confirmation of the auditor or a separate audit of this version. Smart contract auditing helps identify code errors and architectural dependencies. It does not guarantee: constant availability of liquidity; execution of each future Claim; economic sustainability of the model; absence of administrative, market and user risks; security of code versions that were not part of the checked set of files. 2 2. Current register of contracts and infrastructure The registry below is intended to help the reader understand which addresses apply to the current Atlas architecture. This is a separate task from defining audit boundaries. 2.1. Atlas Contracts Component Purpose Address Lockup Flow Smart Cycle with a set deadline and Claim after the cycle conditions are met 0x8F6daC6F25A5038112E1A01f1cBBD682e4D64889

Page 3
Component Purpose Address Daily Flow V2 Current Daily Flow with daily calculation and current commission logic Transport Service output USDT from the general LP position for the partner payment circuit Distribute Affiliate payments from your own balance USDT 2.2. Liquidity and external contracts Component Purpose Address or ID SAFE Atlas Owner LP-NFT and main contracts management loop LP-position Atlas Total concentrated liquidity position PancakeSwap V3 Nonfungible Position Manager External contract PancakeSwap, managing LP-NFT Pool PancakeSwap V3 USDT/USDC Public pool in which the Atlas position and positions of other suppliers are located USDT BEP-20 Atlas main settlement token USDC BEP-20 Second token of the LP pair 0x8e61483d45a822cCB59482c47e1b6D28465605EC 0x5a71807861dBFc41aB016271C3191bF96322D42e 0xEF156690b98AEc4F805Ec820268B9092bd83B76f 0xB0E4699710f98BB13fDaAB887a5D821eDb5DB559 tokenId 6928212 0x46A15B0b27311cedF172AB29E4f4766fbE7F4364 0x92b7807bF19b7DDdf89b706143896d05228f3121 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d

Page 4
2.3. Administrative addresses Component Purpose Address Treasury Receiving commissions sent by Atlas contracts Owner Distribute Address authorized to trigger payments from Distribute SAFE signer 1 One of the on-chain signatories SAFE SAFE signer 2 One of the on-chain signatories SAFE SAFE signer 3 One of the on-chain signatories SAFE At the time of the control shot SAFE used the scheme 2-of-3 : two out of three confirmations were required to complete the operation. This reduces the dependency on a single key, but does not eliminate the SAFE authority. 2.4. How the components are connected Participant Lockup Flow Daily Flow V2 PancakeSwap V3 owner SAFE Atlas 2-of-3 pool USDT / USDC 0x20Cdf9839faC80cCDC38CE74D41bD55A93DD87F2 0x4c7445C39ee62d3F798f9Fd6a61e9399E3dc8Fae 0x7709e4eDcC55714F83027EF39062d7f9761273B6 0x14F9b2cE2850057CAd8e1A9cFeD6eedA777D1C44 0xD067C66C9f4D16130B118929B7BB7Fec5C6FD051 LP-NFT #6928212

Page 5
Transport Distribute partner commission Treasury Several custom orders use one LP position. Balance Distribute, fees Treasury, total public pool liquidity, and the assets of a specific Atlas LP position are different measures. They cannot be added together and called one number without a separate methodology. 3 3. How to read the explanations The same structure is used for each of the 20 comments: Auditor ’ s Note - what exactly is recorded in the report. 01 In simple words is the practical meaning of the technical formulation. 02 Atlas Official Explanation - why the corresponding mechanics exist or how they are configured. 03 What is important to understand - persisting condition, constraint or dependency. 04

Page 6
4 4. Auditor ’ s observations and clarifications Atlas 01 4.1. FRM - First-Come Reward Model Criticality in the report: Critical Status in the report: Unresolved Auditor ’ s note. Lockup Flow and Daily Flow pay out funds from the common position PancakeSwap V3. A separate reserve is not created for each order. Therefore, earlier successful Claim can use the liquidity that later participants rely on. In simple words. The order record shows how much and under what conditions should be paid to the participant, but this record does not mean that the required amount lies separately and is waiting only for him. Funds from different orders work through one common position. Atlas official explanation. The general position is used deliberately: Smart Cycle is a redistribution mechanism with general liquidity, and not a system of individual deposit boxes. The order fixes the rules of a particular cycle, but does not create a personal wallet or a separate reserve. What is important to understand. The Claim capability depends on the actual state of the overall position and the order of executed transactions. The settlement amount for the order is not equal to the personally reserved amount.

Page 7
02 4.2. AOW - Arbitrary Owner Withdrawal Criticality in the report: Medium Status in the report: Unresolved Auditor ’ s note. Function claimReferral() in Transport allows the owner to specify the recipient address and withdrawal amount from the shared LP position. In Transport itself there is no on-chain accounting for partner accruals, limits or proof of entitlement to the specified amount. In simple words. The authorized owner of Transport can technically request the withdrawal of the selected amount to the selected address. The contract itself does not check whether the transaction matches the entry for a specific affiliate reward. Atlas official explanation. Transport is a service contract. It is used to move funds to the partner payment circuit, after which Distribute makes final payments from its balance. Transport is controlled via SAFE 2-of-3 , and not with one regular key. What is important to understand. SAFE reduces the risk of compromising a single key, but does not limit the authority of the code itself. Transport does not record Distribute as the only possible recipient, so the signing procedure and public monitoring of transactions remain a trust boundary.

Page 8
03 4.3. CRD - Claims Range Dependent Criticality in the report: Medium Status in the report: Unresolved Auditor ’ s note. Adding and removing liquidity is only allowed when the current tick is on the expected side of the LP position ’ s range. If the price enters the range, Claim or the withdrawal may end revert . In simple words. Even if the order has expired, the contract first checks the position status PancakeSwap. If the price position is inappropriate, the operation is not performed. Atlas official explanation. Atlas position is configured out of range on the USDT side. This configuration was chosen for regular one-way work with USDT, and not for constant market making within the range. What is important to understand. The setting reduces the likelihood of blocking during normal movement of the USDT/USDC pair, but does not eliminate it completely. A strong depeg, range change, or other change in pool state may temporarily render Claim unavailable. 04 4.4. CCR - Contract Centralization Risk Criticality in the report: Minor / Informative Status in the report: Unresolved Auditor ’ s note. In contracts there are owner functions that allow you to change Treasury, the commission size and the used tokenId . The operation of the system depends on the external configuration and actions of authorized addresses. In simple words. Some important parameters are not fixed forever. The administration can change them through an authorized on-chain transaction. Atlas official explanation. Atlas does not claim that the current version is fully decentralized. Controlled parameters allow you to maintain the infrastructure and change the working LP position. The main contracts and LP-NFT are controlled by SAFE 2-of-3 ; Distribute has a separate owner. What is important to understand. Multi-signature reduces the risk of a single key, but does not override administrative authority. Changes to parameters must be verified on the blockchain.

Page 9
05 4.5. ELFM - Exceeds Fees Limit Criticality in the report: Minor / Informative Status in the report: Unresolved Auditor ’ s note. Function setFee() allows commission setting up to 100% since the upper bound is PRECISION . In simple words. The code does not limit the commission to a small predetermined maximum. An authorized owner can technically set the value to a very high value. Atlas official explanation. In the current configuration, custom Flow and Distribute use commission 10% , and Transport - 0% . For master contracts, the change is made via SAFE. What is important to understand. Current setting does not remove the possibility of future change. Before a significant operation, the user or analyst can re-read platformFee in BscScan. 06 4.6. IWH - Insufficient Withdrawal Handling Criticality in the report: Minor / Informative Status in the report: Unresolved Auditor ’ s note. _withdrawPool() may return less than the estimated amount. The code of the audited version does not require a strict match between the actually received and the expected value, which is why partial payment, loss of the balance or revert when calculating the commission. In simple words. The contract asks for one amount, but can theoretically receive less from the LP position. Further behavior depends on whether the received quantity is sufficient for calculations. Atlas official explanation. Atlas considers the actual amount received from the total position to be the critical value of the transaction. The clarification does not close the note: strict underpayment protection must be supported by the specific version code and individual tests being used. What is important to understand. You cannot assume that any calculated amount will be automatically withdrawn in full. The current version requires separate checking of behavior with insufficient liquidity and at rounding limits.

Page 10
07 4.7. LBR - Liquidity Base Reduction Criticality in the report: Minor / Informative Status in the report: Unresolved Auditor ’ s note. Each successful Claim reduces the active liquidity of the overall position as funds are withdrawn through decreaseLiquidity . In simple words. Incoming transactions increase the total position, and payments decrease it. Funds are not required to constantly remain in the pool and generate trading commissions. Atlas official explanation. The position decrease at Claim is part of the redistribution mechanics Smart Cycle. The LP position is used as a general on-chain contour for the movement of funds, and not as an immutable reserve. What is important to understand. The size of the active position changes after each incoming and outgoing transaction. The historical volume of deposited funds does not equal the current available liquidity. 08 4.8. MTC - Manipulatable Tick Check Criticality in the report: Minor / Informative Status in the report: Unresolved Auditor ’ s note. The contract uses the current slot0().tick , that is, the spot state of the pool, and not the average TWAP price. Spot tick can be temporarily changed by swaps. In simple words. The decision about the availability of an operation is made based on the current state of the pool at that moment. It is not confirmed by an additional source or averaging over the period. Atlas official explanation. Tick is used as a technical condition of the position side, and not as a price at which the order amount is calculated. The position ’ s range is far from the normal USDT/USDC parity, so a small market movement usually does not change the test result. What is important to understand. The dependence on one spot tick is preserved. Unusual market movement, depeg or economically achievable manipulation may affect the availability of the operation.

Page 11
09 4.9. NOM - NFT Ownership Missing Criticality in the report: Minor / Informative Status in the report: Unresolved Auditor ’ s note. Flow contracts interact with LP-NFT, but do not own it themselves and do not check ownership before each operation. Without Position Manager permission, calls may end revert . In simple words. A contract can work with a general position only as long as its owner allows it to do so. Atlas official explanation. This is the custody model used: LP-NFT #6928212 belongs to SAFE Atlas, and work contracts are issued operator approval . The NFT is not transferred ownership to every Flow contract. What is important to understand. SAFE may revoke permission or transfer LP-NFT. The corresponding contract will then lose access to the position and related operations will stop. 10 4.10. NFU - Non-USDT Fees Unhandled Criticality in the report: Minor / Informative Status in the report: Unresolved Auditor ’ s note. collect() can return both tokens of a pair, but the audited logic only considers and translates the configured target token. The second token may remain outside the user calculation. In simple words. The position consists of USDT and USDC. If a contract receives USDC, the code will not necessarily treat it the same way as USDT. Atlas official explanation. The standard script is designed for the position of the position on the USDT-side. Therefore, the main product logic works with USDT. What is important to understand. The out-of-range position itself is not software processing of the second token. An unexpectedly received USDC requires separate accounting and a clear procedure for further actions.

Page 12
11 4.11. NTC - Non-USDT Token Control Criticality in the report: Minor / Informative Status in the report: Unresolved Auditor ’ s note. If the second token of an LP pair is controlled by the owner or a trusted party, a change in its supply may affect the price, tick, availability Claim and position value. In simple words. The system depends not only on USDT, but also on the second token of the pair. Problems with the second token can change the state of the pool. Atlas official explanation. In the current public pool, the second token is USDC. Atlas does not issue or manage the issuance of USDC, so Atlas cannot mint, burn, or change the supply of this token on its own. What is important to understand. The risks of the issuer USDC, blocking of tokens, depeg and external infrastructure remain. Atlas' lack of control does not mean there is no external risk. 12 4.12. PAI - Possible Approval Incompatibility Criticality in the report: Minor / Informative Status in the report: Unresolved Auditor ’ s note. The normal Position Manager resolution is used approve() . Some non- standard ERC-20 require a different sequence and may reject such a call. In simple words. The code may not be compatible with some uncommon tokens, especially if they require the old permission to be reset first. Atlas official explanation. Smart Cycle works with a fixed official USDT BEP-20, not an arbitrary user-selected token. This reduces the practical applicability of the scenario. What is important to understand. A limited list of tokens does not change the implementation itself approve() . Compatibility and re-operations with allowance must be checked on the current version of the contract.

Page 13
13 4.13. PDFD - Possible Double Fee Deduction Criticality in the report: Minor / Informative Status in the report: Unresolved Auditor ’ s note. Both Transport and Distribute contain separate commission logic. If both contracts use a non-zero commission in the same payout chain, the commission may be deducted twice. In simple words. One affiliate payment goes through two contracts. If each of them withdraws their commission, the partner will receive less than the expected amount. Atlas official explanation. In the current configuration, Transport uses fee 0% and transfers the amount to Distribute. Distribute holds 10% at final payment. With this configuration, the commission in the affiliate circuit is deducted once. What is important to understand. Commission values are changeable parameters. No double hold depends on maintaining the current configuration. 14 4.14. PTAI - Potential Transfer Amount Inconsistency Criticality in the report: Minor / Informative Status in the report: Unresolved Auditor ’ s note. Fee-on-transfer token may actually transfer less than specified transferFrom() . If the contract takes into account the amount requested rather than the amount actually received, a discrepancy arises. In simple words. The user sends a conditional 100 tokens, but the transfer tax token can only deliver 90 to the contract. Atlas official explanation. The current model uses the official USDT BEP-20, which does not apply transfer tax in normal Atlas operation. The contract is not intended for arbitrary tax tokens. What is important to understand. The applicability of the note is reduced by the selected token, but a correct accounting system should still be based on the amount actually received.

Page 14
15 4.15. RLW - Rounded Liquidity Withdrawal Criticality in the report: Minor / Informative Status in the report: Unresolved Auditor ’ s note. After calculating the liquidity volume, the code adds one. This may result in an attempt to withdraw a little more than necessary, an additional withdrawal, or a complete revert at the border of available liquidity. In simple words. The contract rounds the calculation up to avoid receiving less due to rounding down. But at the very edge of the position, even one extra unit can make a difference. Atlas official explanation. Adding one is used to compensate for the peculiarities of integer mathematics PancakeSwap V3. The surplus target token in the audited logic is sent to Treasury as position reward. What is important to understand. Rounding compensation does not guarantee successful output. Boundary values, accumulated commissions and insufficient liquidity should be checked by separate tests. 16 4.16. SMC - Strict Maturity Check Criticality in the report: Minor / Informative Status in the report: Unresolved Auditor ’ s note. Lockup Flow allows Claim only when block.timestamp is strictly greater than the completion time, not equal to it. In simple words. At the exact second of the deadline, Claim is not yet available. You need to wait for the next block with a later time. Atlas official explanation. This is a time comparison feature in the code. It does not change the recipient ’ s address or transfer the Claim right to another person. What is important to understand. The actual availability of a transaction always depends on the time of the next block. The interface should not promise execution at the exact second.

Page 15
17 4.17. URR - Unrealistic Reward Rates Criticality in the report: Minor / Informative Status in the report: Unresolved Auditor ’ s note. The contracts specify high fixed settlement values, and a guaranteed external source of income that sustainably finances payments is not defined in the code. In simple words. The formula can calculate the amount, but the formula itself does not create money or reserve it for future payment. Atlas official explanation. The percentages Smart Cycle are parameters of the redistribution model. Atlas does not attribute them to guaranteed income from trading, mining or LP fees, and does not represent them as guaranteed investment returns. What is important to understand. Calculated Delta is not equal to the guaranteed result. The possibility of payment depends on the overall liquidity and the actual operation of the mechanism. 18 4.18. L04 - Conformance to Solidity Naming Conventions Criticality in the report: Minor / Informative Status in the report: Unresolved Auditor ’ s note. Some names and design elements of the source code do not fully comply with the Solidity Style Guide. In simple words. The code can be formatted more consistently to make it easier for third-party developers to read and maintain. Atlas official explanation. This note relates to the quality and support of the sources. It does not change the bytecode of an already deployed contract and does not itself describe a separate method for withdrawing funds. What is important to understand. Code readability affects the quality of future changes and reviews, so the note remains useful even without directly affecting the current transaction.

Page 16
19 4.19. L13 - Divide before Multiply Operation Criticality in the report: Minor / Informative Status in the report: Unresolved Auditor ’ s note. In Daily Flow part of the calculation is division before subsequent multiplication. In Solidity integer arithmetic, this may prematurely discard the fractional part. In simple words. If you first round a number down and then multiply, the result will sometimes be slightly less than if you did the opposite. Atlas official explanation. The calculation is deterministic: the same input data gives the same result. However, the accuracy of the minimum token units must be consistent with the published formula and display in the interface. What is important to understand. The note applies to the audited version of Daily Flow. For the current Daily Flow V2 the order of calculation and the result must be checked separately against its source code. 20 4.20. L19 - Stable Compiler Version Criticality in the report: Minor / Informative Status in the report: Unresolved Auditor ’ s note. Used in source codes pragma solidity ^0.8.20 , so different compatible versions of the compiler can compile different bytecode. In simple words. If you compile the same code with a different compiler in the future, the resulting contract may differ. Atlas official explanation. Already expanded bytecode does not change due to recording pragma . For a repeatable build, it is important to record the exact compiler version, optimizer options, and dependencies for each deployment. What is important to understand. Status Contract: Verified in BscScan allows you to match published source code to a specific bytecode, but does not replace a reproducible build and security audit.

1 1. О документе и границах аудита Cyberscope проверил набор исходных файлов PositionHandler.sol , Transport.sol , LockupFlow.sol , DailyFlow.sol , Distrib.sol и связанных интерфейсов. В версии отчёта Corrected Phase 2 указано 20 замечаний: 1 Critical; 2 Medium; 17 Minor / Informative. ОФИЦИАЛЬНЫЙ ДОКУМЕНТ Пояснение Atlas System к аудиту Cyberscope Отчёт: Cyberscope, Corrected Phase 2 Дата отчёта: 30 июня 2026 года Сеть: BNB Smart Chain Версия пояснения: 2.0 Дата пояснения: 25 июля 2026 года Это официальный комментарий Atlas System к каждому замечанию аудитора. Документ не опровергает аудит, не меняет присвоенную критичность и не объявляет замечания закрытыми. Его задача - перевести технические формулировки на понятный язык и объяснить, как соответствующая часть системы устроена в Atlas.

Page 2
Все 20 замечаний отмечены аудитором как Unresolved . Настоящее пояснение не меняет этот статус. Если Atlas описывает фактическую настройку, которая снижает применимость отдельного сценария, это является пояснением текущей конфигурации, а не самостоятельным закрытием замечания. Аудит относится к конкретным исходным файлам и их SHA-256, перечисленным в отчёте от 30 июня 2026 года. После этой даты архитектура могла получить новые deployments или изменённые версии контрактов. В частности, текущий адрес Daily Flow V2 включён в актуальный реестр, но не должен автоматически считаться проверенным июньским отчётом без отдельного подтверждения аудитора или отдельного аудита этой версии. Аудит смарт-контрактов помогает выявлять ошибки кода и архитектурные зависимости. Он не гарантирует: постоянное наличие ликвидности; выполнение каждого будущего Claim; экономическую устойчивость модели; отсутствие административных, рыночных и пользовательских рисков; безопасность версий кода, которые не входили в проверенный набор файлов. 2 2. Актуальный реестр контрактов и инфраструктуры Реестр ниже нужен, чтобы читатель понимал, какие адреса относятся к текущей архитектуре Atlas. Это отдельная задача от определения границ аудита. 2.1. Это снижает зависимость от одного ключа, но не устраняет полномочия SAFE. 2.4.
