sources.content:
1. Interface map

The main navigation remains available across the personal dashboard. Before performing an action, make sure the correct wallet and language are selected.

Top bar

Element

What it shows

Why it matters

Days in the system

Time since the wallet first connected to Atlas System

Shows the participation age associated with the connected wallet

Voting Balance

Votes currently available for governance mechanics

Terminology defines 10 USDT of participation as 1 vote

Connected wallet

Shortened address of the active wallet

Always compare it with the wallet you intend to use before creating a cycle or making a Claim

Language

Current interface language

Changes the language of the personal dashboard

Notifications

Access to system messages

Opens All, Read and Unread messages

The connected wallet address is intentionally excluded from the guide screenshots.

Side navigation

Section

What it is for

Dashboard

Overview of personal activity, active cycles and partner indicators

Provide Support

Creation of a new Lockup Flow or Daily Flow cycle

My Support Cycles

Active cycles, completed cycles and Operations History

Partner Program

Partner wallet, accruals, team structure and statistics

Profile

Personal information, contacts, visibility and communication settings

How to move around the dashboard

Select a section in the left menu.

Check the connected wallet before any transaction-related action.

Use the language selector if the interface is not displayed in the required language.

Return to Dashboard whenever you need a general overview.

Use Logout when you finish working on a shared or public device.

What to check

The official domain is app.atlas-system.io.

The expected wallet is connected.

BNB Smart Chain is selected for transaction-related actions.

No person or support representative should request your seed phrase or private key.

The screenshot begins below the top bar so that the participant's wallet address is not displayed. It focuses only on the side navigation and System Health panel. The main Dashboard area is shown separately in the next visual.

2. Dashboard

What it is

Dashboard is the main overview screen. It summarises the participant's cycles, activity, available assistance and partner progress without requiring the user to open each section separately.

Why it is needed

Use Dashboard to:

see the number of active and completed cycles;

compare Lockup Flow and Daily Flow activity;

check received and expected Delta;

see whether assistance is currently available;

review total support, assistance and partner rewards;

open current cycles or partner information for more detail.

Main summary cards

Total cycles

Shows the number of Active / Completed cycles.

Active — cycles currently running under their smart contract conditions.

Completed — cycles that have finished under the rules of the selected flow.

A newly created cycle may take a short time to appear while the blockchain transaction is being confirmed.

Active Cycle Volume

Shows the active Support Amount broken down by Lockup Flow / Daily Flow.

This is the value assigned to active cycles. It is not the spendable USDT balance in the connected wallet.

Delta

Shows Received / Expected Delta.

Received Delta — additional assistance already received above the amount of provided support.

Expected Delta — additional assistance calculated under the current Smart Cycle conditions.

Expected Delta is a calculation, not a guaranteed balance. Availability depends on the smart contract rules and available liquidity.

Assistance Available

Shows the amount currently available to request through Claim.

Before making a Claim, check:

the relevant cycle;

connected wallet;

BNB Smart Chain network;

BNB balance for gas;

the amount shown in the wallet confirmation.

Your Atlas System Activity

This block compares three types of participant activity:

Indicator

Meaning

Support Provided

Total amount of support directed into Smart Cycles

Assistance Received

Assistance already received through completed Claims

Partner Rewards

Rewards received through the Partner Program

These figures represent different categories and should not be added together as if they were a wallet balance.

My Active Cycles

This block provides quick access to current cycles. Open My Support Cycles when you need the full cycle card, dates, terms, status, Expected Delta, Claim action or transaction information.

If there are no active cycles, the block may be empty.

Partner Status

The Dashboard shows a compact partner summary:

Current Partner Status;

Personal Active Cycle Volume;

First-Line Active Cycle Volume;

Partner Structure Active Cycle Volume;

remaining requirements for the next status.

The detailed qualification rules, Team Delta Volume, structure coefficients and reward examples belong in the separate Partner Program guide.

How to use Dashboard

Open Dashboard in the side menu.

Check the four summary cards at the top.

Review the activity block to distinguish support, assistance and partner rewards.

Open My Active Cycles if a cycle requires attention.

Open the Partner Program section when the partner summary requires more detail.

What to check when values look incorrect

Confirm that the same wallet used for the operation is connected.

Wait for blockchain confirmation and refresh the page.

Compare the information with My Support Cycles → Operations History.

Verify the transaction on BscScan.

If the confirmed transaction is still missing, contact support and provide the transaction hash.

Numeric values shown in screenshots are examples and may change at any time.

3. Provide Support

What it is

Provide Support is the section used to create a new Smart Cycle. It contains the same basic sequence for both modes: select a flow, review its conditions, enter the Support Amount, accept the terms and confirm the transaction in the connected wallet.

Use this section when you are ready to create a cycle. To review an existing cycle or make a Claim, open My Support Cycles instead.

Why it is needed

Provide Support allows the participant to:

choose between Lockup Flow and Daily Flow;

select or identify the applicable cycle tariff;

specify the Support Amount in USDT;

review Expected Assistance before confirming;

confirm voluntary participation and the terms of use;

send the transaction request to the connected wallet.

Fields available in both modes

Field

What it means

What to check

Choose Cycle Type

Selects Lockup Flow or Daily Flow

Make sure the required mode is highlighted

Select Cycle

Shows the selected tariff and its conditions

Check the tariff name, term and calculation

Support Amount, USDT

Amount of support directed into the cycle

Use USDT on BNB Smart Chain and check the minimum amount

Expected Assistance (Principal + Delta)

Calculated principal and additional assistance

Treat this as a calculation under the smart contract rules, not a guaranteed wallet balance

Terms of use

Rules governing participation

Open and read the terms before accepting

Voluntary confirmation

Confirms that the participant is acting voluntarily

Both confirmations are required before the button becomes available

Provide Support

Sends the operation to the connected wallet

The cycle is not created until the wallet transaction is confirmed

3.1 Lockup Flow

What it is

Lockup Flow creates a cycle with a fixed term. Assistance becomes available for Claim after the selected term ends, subject to the relevant smart contract rules and available liquidity.

What is shown

Lockup Flow — Assistance at Term End selector;

cycle tariff with its term and calculated percentage;

Support Amount in USDT;

Expected Assistance shown as Principal + Delta;

required confirmations;

Provide Support button;

notice that the cycle is created only after wallet confirmation.

The Contract Test tariff uses a fixed Support Amount of 10 USDT. Its purpose is to let the participant test the full interaction with the smart contract over a short period. Other Lockup Flow tariffs use their own terms and calculations.

Available Lockup Flow cycles

Cycle

Term

Calculated Delta

Contract Test

10 minutes

Launch

+0.3%

Momentum

+2%

Premiere

10 days

+5%

20 days

+12%

Imperium

30 days

+22.5%

The open selector in the screenshot shows all six options together. Before choosing, compare the term and calculated Delta with the amount you are prepared to direct into the cycle.

How to use it

Open Provide Support.

Select Lockup Flow.

Open Select Cycle and choose the required tariff.

Check the term and calculated percentage shown next to the tariff.

Enter the Support Amount. For Contract Test, the amount is fixed at 10 USDT.

Review Expected Assistance (Principal + Delta).

Open and accept the terms of use.

Confirm that providing support is voluntary.

Click Provide Support.

Verify the network, token, amount and gas fee in the wallet, then confirm the transaction.

3.2 Daily Flow

What it is

Daily Flow creates a 200-day cycle with the right to request assistance daily under the smart contract conditions. The original Support Amount is included in the daily assistance Claims.

What is different from Lockup Flow

the cycle lasts 200 days;

the applicable tariff depends on the Support Amount;

the form shows Daily accrual;

assistance can be requested daily according to the contract conditions;

assistance is not deferred to a single end-of-term Claim.

Current tariff ranges:

Tariff

Support Amount

Term

Daily payout

Calculated Delta

Core

10–2,000 USDT

200 days

1.1% per day

+120%

Elite

Above 2,000 USDT

200 days

1.3% per day

+160%

The interface may determine the Daily Flow tariff automatically according to the entered Support Amount.

The original Support Amount is included in the daily assistance Claims. The daily payout and Delta shown in the interface are calculations under the current smart contract conditions and available liquidity.

How to use it

Open Provide Support.

Select Daily Flow.

Check the tariff displayed in Select Cycle.

Enter the Support Amount. The current minimum is 10 USDT.

Review Expected Assistance (Principal + Delta) and Daily accrual.

Open and accept the terms of use.

Confirm that providing support is voluntary.

Click Provide Support.

Verify the transaction details in the wallet and confirm.

After blockchain confirmation, open My Support Cycles to check the new cycle.

The combined visual shows the Daily Flow form first and the Core/Elite comparison directly below it.

3.3 Wallet confirmation

The Provide Support button does not move funds by itself. It creates a transaction request that must be reviewed and signed in the connected wallet.

Before confirming, check:

the wallet is connected to BNB Smart Chain;

the token is USDT BEP-20;

the Support Amount matches the form;

the wallet contains enough BNB for gas;

the destination is the official Atlas System smart contract;

the transaction was opened from app.atlas-system.io.

For the first USDT operation, the wallet may request two confirmations:

USDT approval for the smart contract;

creation of the Smart Cycle.

Both transactions require BNB gas. Never enter a seed phrase or private key into the Atlas System website.

If the button is unavailable

Check that:

the Support Amount meets the minimum and tariff limits;

both confirmations are selected;

the wallet is connected;

the correct network is active;

the form does not show a validation error.

Lockup Flow tariffs, Daily Flow calculations, cycle statuses and Claim are covered in the separate Smart Cycle guide.

4. My Support Cycles

What it is

My Support Cycles is the section for monitoring cycles after they have been created. It separates current cycles, finished cycles and the history of cycle creation and received assistance.

Use this section to:

confirm that a new cycle appeared after the blockchain transaction;

track active Lockup Flow and Daily Flow cycles;

check terms, dates and calculated Delta;

find completed cycles;

review cycle creation and assistance history;

locate information needed for BscScan verification or a support request.

The section contains three main tabs: Active, Completed and Operations History.

4.1 Active

What it shows

The Active tab contains cycles that are currently running under their smart contract conditions.

The upper flow selector separates:

Lockup Flow — Assistance at Term End;

Daily Flow — Daily Assistance.

Summary indicators:

Indicator

Meaning

Active Cycle Volume

Total Support Amount currently assigned to active cycles of the selected flow

Expected Delta

Calculated additional assistance for the active cycles shown

Cycle information may include:

Support Amount;

terms;

start and end date;

Expected Delta;

current status;

available Claim action;

related blockchain transaction.

How to use it

Open My Support Cycles → Active.

Select Lockup Flow or Daily Flow.

Find the required cycle by its Support Amount, term or date.

Check the current status and calculation.

If Claim is available, review the amount and confirm the transaction in the wallet.

For Daily Flow, the available assistance may change according to the daily calculation and completed Claims.

4.2 Completed

What it shows

The Completed tab contains cycles that have finished under the rules of the selected flow and are no longer shown as active.

Summary indicators:

Indicator

Meaning

Completed Cycle Volume

Total Support Amount associated with completed cycles of the selected flow

Received Delta

Delta already received from the completed cycles shown

The same Lockup Flow and Daily Flow selector is available. Historical cycle information remains useful for checking the Support Amount, term, dates, calculation and related transactions.

How to use it

Open My Support Cycles → Completed.

Select the required flow.

Find the cycle by amount, term or dates.

Compare its information with Operations History.

Use the transaction information for independent verification on BscScan.

The combined visual shows Active first and Completed directly below it. The sample wallet has no cycles, so the screenshots demonstrate the empty states and available controls without exposing participant data.

4.3 Operations History

Operations History records the two main types of participant activity related to Smart Cycles.

Cycle Creation

Use this tab to check the cycles that were created from the connected wallet.

Displayed fields:

Cycle Creation Date;

Cycle Name;

Terms;

Support Amount.

This view is useful when a cycle creation transaction was confirmed but the participant needs to check when and under which conditions the cycle was created.

Assistance Received

Use this tab to review completed assistance Claims.

Summary indicators:

Assistance Claims Received;

Assistance Received Volume.

Displayed fields:

Cycle;

Cycle Creation Date;

Payout Amount;

Smart Contract;

Status.

The Smart contract and Status fields help connect the dashboard record with on-chain verification.

The combined visual shows Cycle Creation first and Assistance Received below it.

4.4 If a cycle or operation is missing

Confirm that the same wallet used for the transaction is connected.

Check that BNB Smart Chain is selected.

Wait for blockchain confirmation and refresh the personal dashboard.

Check both Lockup Flow and Daily Flow filters.

Check Active, Completed and Operations History.

Open the transaction in the wallet or BscScan.

connected wallet address;

transaction hash;

cycle type and amount;

approximate operation time;

screenshot of the relevant tab.

Cycle statuses and Claim conditions are explained in Smart Cycle. Transaction verification is covered in Contracts & BscScan.

5. Partner Program

The Partner Program section brings together partner rewards, team structure, status progress and activity statistics. Use it to monitor your own partner account and the activity associated with your referral structure.

This section explains the personal dashboard interface. Status rules, Team Delta Volume, reward calculation and worked examples are covered in the separate Partner Program guide.

The section contains four tabs:

Partner Wallet;

Accrual History;

My Team;

Statistics.

5.1 Partner Wallet

Partner Wallet shows the current state of partner rewards.

Indicator

Meaning

Account Balance

Partner rewards currently shown as available in the dashboard

Total Accrued

Total partner rewards accrued under the program rules

Rewards Received

Partner rewards already received

The Withdrawal History table records withdrawals and displays:

Withdrawal date;

Withdrawal amount;

Status;

Tx Hash.

Use Tx Hash to open the related transaction on BscScan and verify it independently. The information tooltip next to Account Balance explains how automatic payouts work.

5.2 Accrual History

Accrual History shows how partner rewards were accrued. When accruals are available, the table includes:

Accrual Date;

Bonus;

Accrued Reward Amount.

Use this tab when you need to identify the bonus that created an accrual. An accrued reward and a received payout are different stages: first check the accrual here, then check the Partner Wallet and its Withdrawal History.

The combined visual shows Partner Wallet first and Accrual History directly below it.

5.3 My Team

My Team is the main workspace for status progress and referral structure.

Partner information

The upper panel displays:

Partner Status — the current status and its reward rate;

My Referral Link — the personal link used to invite new participants;

My Referrer (Wallet Address) — the wallet whose referral link was used;

Referrer Status — the current status of that referrer.

The personal referral link becomes available after the first qualifying Smart Cycle of 10 USDT or more. If the field shows Not Available, check the cycle and status conditions described in the Partner Program guide.

Requirements for Next Status

Progress is shown for three volumes:

Personal Active Cycle Volume;

First-Line Active Cycle Volume;

Partner Structure Active Cycle Volume.

For each requirement, compare Current, Required and Remaining. This makes it clear which condition has already been met and which volume is still needed for the next status.

Status Requirements and structure

The Status Requirements table compares all statuses by:

personal active cycle volume;

first-line active cycle volume;

partner structure active cycle volume;

structure reward rate with unlimited depth;

matching reward rate.

Below the table, use Structure Lines and Search by Wallet Address to navigate the structure. The results identify the participant wallet and status. The Leaders statistics in the structure section helps identify the most active parts of the team.

The screenshot uses an account without an active partner status and does not expose a participant wallet address.

5.4 Statistics

Statistics summarizes partner activity for the selected period. Available filters are Day, Week, Month, Year and All Time.

Partners

New Registrations (Wallet Connected) — wallets newly connected through the structure;

Active Partners (Wallet Connected + Cycle Created) — connected partners who also created a cycle.

Cycles created

Lockup Flow and Daily Flow are shown separately. For each flow, the dashboard groups activity by:

Entire Structure;

First Line;

Lines 2–10;

Line 11+.

The tables show the number of cycles, the amount in USDT and the total volume included in the system metrics.

How structure depth affects full volume

The information tooltip next to Total volume explains the coefficients used for structure depth:

Structure depth

Volume counted

First Line

100% for the first-line and unlimited-depth metrics

Lines 2–5

100% for the unlimited-depth metric

Lines 6–10

50%

Line 11+

10%

Most Active Lines highlights the leading structure lines and shows their partner count and USDT volume.

5.5 Important notes

Account Balance in Partner Wallet is a dashboard partner balance; it is not the same as the USDT balance displayed by your wallet application.

New accruals, withdrawals and statistics may appear after blockchain confirmation and dashboard synchronization.

Always check that the correct wallet is connected before reviewing partner data.

Do not publish referral or participant wallet data in screenshots without consent.

For an on-chain check, use the transaction hash and the official contract registry.

Status conditions, Team Delta Volume and reward examples are explained in Partner Program. Terms are defined in Terminology.

6. Profile

The Profile section stores the participant information used for communication and partner-facing features. It does not store wallet access credentials and does not replace the connected wallet address.

Open Profile from the left navigation. After making changes, select Save at the bottom of the page.

6.1 General Information

The upper panel contains:

Avatar — select the camera icon to add or replace the profile image;

Status — the current partner status associated with the connected wallet;

Full Name;

Country;

City.

The interface warns that the uploaded photo may be shown on the participant's partner landing page. Use only an image that you are comfortable displaying there.

6.2 Contact Information

This section contains Phone Number and Email.

The Visible to partners switch controls the partner visibility setting for the contact information block. Before enabling it, check that the entered details are intended to be shared with partners.

6.3 Social Networks

The available fields are:

Facebook — username or profile link;

Instagram — username or profile link;

WhatsApp — phone number or link;

Telegram — username, link or phone number.

Social networks have their own Visible to partners switch. This setting is separate from the visibility switch in Contact Information.

You can leave fields empty if you do not use a service or do not want it included in your profile.

6.4 Communication Settings

Communication Language

Communication Language records the participant's preferred language for communication. Select one of the supported Atlas System languages listed in Notifications and interface language below.

This field is different from the language selector in the top bar: the top-bar control changes the dashboard interface language, while Communication Language belongs to the saved profile settings.

Preferred Communication Method

Select the channels through which you prefer to communicate:

Telegram;

WhatsApp;

Email.

Complete the corresponding contact or social-network field before selecting a preferred method. More than one checkbox can be selected when several channels are suitable.

Select Save after changing the language, communication methods or any other profile field.

6.5 Privacy and security

Enable Visible to partners only for information you intend to share.

Use the two visibility switches independently: one applies to contact details and the other to social networks.

Never enter a seed phrase, private key, wallet password, one-time security code or exchange password in any profile field.

Atlas System support does not need wallet access credentials to check a profile issue.

The shortened wallet address in the top bar identifies the connected wallet; it is not edited from Profile.

6.6 If changes are not saved

Confirm that all required fields use the expected format.

Select Save and wait for the interface response.

Refresh the page and check whether the values remain.

Confirm that the same wallet is still connected.

If the values disappear again, contact support and attach a screenshot without exposing private credentials.

Partner status and the partner landing page are explained in Partner Program. Safe data sharing is covered in Security.

7. Notifications and interface language

The notification bell and interface language selector are located in the top bar and remain available throughout the personal dashboard.

7.1 Notifications

Select the Notifications bell to open the notification center. Messages are grouped into three tabs:

Tab

What it shows

All messages

All available notifications

Read

Notifications that have already been opened or marked as read

Unread

Notifications that have not yet been read; the number in brackets is the current unread count

If the page shows You have no notifications yet, there are currently no messages for the connected account. This is a normal empty state and does not indicate an error.

Important limitation

A dashboard notification is informational. It does not replace:

wallet transaction status;

blockchain confirmation;

the transaction record on BscScan;

the current cycle status in My Support Cycles.

When a notification and an on-chain transaction appear inconsistent, verify the wallet address, transaction hash and smart contract first.

7.2 Interface language

Select the current language in the top bar, then choose the required interface language:

English;

Bahasa Indonesia;

Bahasa Melayu;

Deutsch;

Español;

Français;

Русский;

Português;

Tiếng Việt;

Türkçe;

हिन्दी;

中文;

ไทย.

The selected option changes the language of the Atlas System personal dashboard. The wallet extension, BscScan and other external services keep their own language settings.

The combined visual shows the notification tabs on the left and the complete interface language list on the right. The example account has no notifications.

7.3 Interface language vs Communication Language

These two settings serve different purposes:

Setting

Location

Purpose

Interface language

Top bar

Changes the language used by the personal dashboard interface

Communication Language

Profile

Records the participant's preferred language for communication

If you want both settings to match, change the top-bar language and then select the same language in Profile → Communication Language and save the profile.

7.4 If notifications or translations do not update

Confirm that the correct wallet is connected.

Refresh the dashboard.

Reopen the notification center or language selector.

Check whether the selected language is shown in the top bar.

If an expected message is missing, verify the related cycle or transaction in the relevant dashboard section and on BscScan.

Contact support if the dashboard remains inconsistent, providing a screenshot and transaction hash when applicable.

Official translated labels are collected in Terminology. Related issues are covered in Troubleshooting.

8. System Health: Last 24 Hours

The System Health: Last 24 Hours panel is located below the main navigation. It provides an at-a-glance view of system-wide activity and operational status.

These indicators describe Atlas System as a whole. They are not the connected participant's wallet balance, personal cycle volume or guaranteed assistance amount.

8.1 Indicators

Indicator

What it means

Server Time

The date and time used by the dashboard when presenting the current health snapshot

Cycles Created / Incoming Support Volume

Number of cycles created and their combined incoming Support Volume for the displayed period

Cycles Completed / Outgoing Assistance Volume

Number of completed cycles and their combined outgoing Assistance Volume for the displayed period

System Reserve Balance

The system-wide reserve value shown by the dashboard; it is not the participant's wallet or dashboard balance

New Wallets Connected

Number of newly connected wallets recorded for the displayed period

Contracts

Current dashboard status of the Atlas System smart contracts, such as Active

Last Assistance Claim

Time elapsed since the latest recorded assistance Claim in the system

Liquidity Pool

Current dashboard health status of the liquidity pool, such as OK

For the two cycle indicators, the first value is the number of cycles and the second value is the USDT volume.

The screenshot shows the complete System Health panel. All numbers are examples from the moment it was captured and will change over time.

8.2 How to interpret the panel

A green overall health shield provides a quick visual summary of the current dashboard state.

Contracts: Active means the dashboard currently reports the contracts as operational.

Liquidity Pool: OK means the dashboard currently reports the pool health check as normal.

Last Assistance Claim is an activity timestamp. A longer interval does not by itself prove that the system is unavailable.

System Reserve Balance and system-wide volumes do not determine whether a specific participant can Claim.

A healthy panel does not replace checking the status of a particular wallet transaction on BscScan.

8.3 If an indicator looks delayed or unavailable

Check Server Time to understand when the displayed snapshot was recorded.

Refresh the dashboard once and review the indicators again.

Open the official System Status page for service-wide incidents or maintenance.

Check the official contract addresses and their recent transactions on BscScan.

For a personal transaction, verify its transaction hash and check My Support Cycles or Operations History.

connected wallet address;

transaction hash, if applicable;

Detailed availability is published in System Status. Official addresses and on-chain verification are covered in Contracts & BscScan.

No matching question

Try a shorter query or open the Troubleshooting guide.

Open the official Atlas System website (atlas-system.io (http://atlas-system.io)), connect MetaMask on the BNB Smart Chain network, and confirm the wallet connection. The first wallet connection creates your Web3 profile in the system. Important: use only the official domain and never share your seed phrase.

No. Login and registration happen through a Web3 wallet, without email or password.

In Web3, an account is defined by the wallet address. So the system sees not a login and password, but the public address you connected with and use to sign actions.

Yes, if the participant has MetaMask Mobile.

If you came by invitation, use the referral link before your first connection, because after registration the inviter cannot be changed.

Check that MetaMask is installed, the selected account, the BNB Smart Chain network, the site permissions in the wallet, and pop-ups. Then refresh the page and reconnect.

Reconnect MetaMask, check the selected account, the BNB Smart Chain network, and the site permissions in the wallet.

Check the official domain manually and don't follow links from private messages. If the link differs from the official one by even a single character, do not connect your wallet.

If the wallet is already registered, changing the inviter is not possible.

Atlas System uses the MetaMask wallet.

You need a wallet on the BNB Smart Chain (BSC) network. If you use USDT, make sure it is USDT on the BEP-20 network.

BNB is needed to pay the BNB Smart Chain network fee when confirming transactions.

A small amount for gas (about $5). The exact fee changes on the network, so check the gas estimate in MetaMask before any action.

Use USDT on BNB Smart Chain (BEP-20) only. Sending through another network may make the assets unavailable to the intended Atlas address and can require specialist recovery steps, if recovery is technically possible at all.

It is the main recovery key for your wallet. It must never be shared with anyone, including support.

No. Atlas does not store private keys and cannot restore access to a wallet. The wallet owner is responsible for keeping the seed phrase safe.

Rely on the blockchain data and the tx hash; the dashboard interface may update with a delay.

In MetaMask, under the account name. The address can be copied and used to verify transactions.

Signing a message usually confirms wallet ownership and login to the dashboard. A transaction with a fee is only needed for blockchain actions: creating a cycle, Claim, and other on-chain operations.

Don't sign the transaction if you don't understand what it does. Verify the site address, the contract address, and the instructions, and contact support before confirming.

A cycle is a scenario of interaction with the Atlas smart contract chosen by the participant, with a set amount, term, and calculated delta. It is not a bank deposit and not a guaranteed investment return.

Connect your wallet, go to the cycles tab, choose a cycle and amount, then confirm the transaction in MetaMask.

The current minimum Support Amount is 10 USDT. Check the Personal Dashboard before confirming because product parameters may be updated.

A cycle is considered active only after the transaction is successfully confirmed on the blockchain and the action is reflected in the smart contract/dashboard.

The transaction may still be pending, or the Personal Dashboard may need time to update. First verify the Tx Hash on BscScan and confirm the wallet and BNB Smart Chain network before creating another cycle.

Check your BNB for gas, the network, your USDT balance, and the error on BscScan. Then contact support with the transaction hash. Don't send private data to support — only the public address and tx hash are needed.

Once the transaction is confirmed on the blockchain, the action cannot be canceled.

Yes, the product rules allow several active or sequential cycles.

An active cycle cannot be topped up. You need to create a new cycle.

Yes, an experienced user can interact with the smart contract directly if the contract address is officially published. This method requires technical understanding and increases the risk of user error.

A blockchain transfer cannot be cancelled after confirmation. Recovery may be impossible and depends on the destination address, so verify the official Contract Address Registry, network and token before confirming.

Atlas has short fixed Smart Cycles and the long-term Daily Flow. Each cycle has its own amount, term, calculated delta, and Claim rules.

A 10-minute test cycle with no delta, used to check the mechanics. Contract Test is only for checking the interface/contract and should not be used as an example of returns. Contract Test can be used only once.

A fixed 1-day cycle with a calculated delta of +0.3% (this is a calculation model, not a guarantee).

A fixed 5-day cycle with a calculated delta of +2% (this is a calculation model, not a guarantee).

A fixed 10-day cycle with a calculated delta of +5% (this is a calculation model, not a guarantee).

A fixed 20-day cycle with a calculated delta of +12% (this is a calculation model, not a guarantee).

A fixed 30-day cycle with a calculated delta of +22.5% (this is a calculation model, not a guarantee).

A long-term 200-day cycle with a daily calculated accrual model.

No. Creating a Smart Cycle is not an investment transaction and does not guarantee the return of the Support Amount or any Delta. Availability depends on the smart-contract rules, participant activity and liquidity.

The received aid depends on the rules of the chosen Smart Cycle, the state of the smart contract, available liquidity, network fees, and the user correctly executing the transactions.

Claim is the on-chain action used to request assistance that the smart contract currently shows as available under the selected Smart Cycle rules.

After the chosen cycle's term ends or when the Daily Flow conditions are met — when the interface shows an available amount to receive.

Claim may send the amount currently available under the selected cycle rules. Claiming the Support Amount or Delta is not guaranteed and depends on the contract conditions and available liquidity.

To the connected wallet of the participant who took part in the cycle.

Yes, to pay the network fee when sending the Claim transaction.

Most often the issue is insufficient BNB for the fee, a network error, or the payout not yet being available.

A repeat Claim is possible when the interface shows an available amount to receive.

Check the transaction on BscScan and wait for confirmation or a failed status.

Yes. After receiving aid, you can immediately create a new cycle.

If the Claim button isn't showing, check the selected wallet, the BNB Smart Chain network, the cycle status, the completion term, and the dashboard sync. Then check the contract/transaction data on BscScan.

Claim Assistance is a transaction on BNB Smart Chain. To process it, the blockchain charges a small network gas fee. The fee can be paid: • directly in BNB; • in USDT, if the connected wallet supports Gas Station or a similar feature. When paying in USDT, the wallet automatically converts the required amount to cover the gas fee. The payment method and exact fee are displayed in the wallet before the transaction is confirmed. The network fee is not charged by Atlas System and is separate from the Platform Fee, which is calculated independently.

Partner Program access is activated automatically after the first qualifying Smart Cycle with a Support Amount of 10 USDT or more.

After activation, the referral link appears in Personal Dashboard → Partner Program → My Team.

Partner Rewards are calculated from Delta generated within the Partner Structure, subject to Partner Status, qualification and compression rules. They are not guaranteed income and are not calculated from the Support Amount itself.

For Lockup Flow, the applicable Partner Reward is accrued when the invited participant creates a Smart Cycle. Daily Flow uses its own staged distribution rules. Check Accrual History for the recorded amount.

Compression distributes the applicable percentage difference through the Partner Structure according to Partner Status. If a lower participant has an equal or higher percentage qualification, the upper participant does not receive a Partner Reward from that structure segment.

These are the participants the partner invited directly.

These are the levels of participants below the first line. Atlas declares unlimited structure depth.

Status depends on personal active volume, first-line volume, structure depth, and status requirements.

Matching Reward becomes available from Master status and may be calculated from Partner Rewards of personally invited participants when the current status and qualification conditions are met.

A recorded Partner Reward can be withdrawn when it is available in Partner Program → Partner Wallet under the active dashboard and smart-contract rules.

There is no automatic reinvestment mechanism. After a Partner Reward reaches the connected wallet, the participant may independently use available funds to create a new Smart Cycle.

The result may reflect Partner Status, compression, Daily Flow distribution timing and the 10% Platform Fee applied to Partner Rewards. Compare the record in Accrual History with the current Partner Program rules.

No. Partner Rewards depend on the current program rules, Partner Status, qualification, structure activity and the underlying Delta.

Yes. Atlas may publish changes as the ecosystem develops. Treat a change as active only after it appears in an official notice, the Personal Dashboard or the applicable smart-contract/interface rules.

There are Start, Builder 1-7, Master 1-7, and the top statuses Strategist, Ambassador, Director, Executive.

Partner Status determines the applicable Partner Reward percentage qualification and, from Master status, the possible Matching Reward percentage under current rules.

You need to meet the requirements for personal active volume and structure according to the status table.

You need to meet higher requirements for personal, first-line, and deep volume.

Status may be recalculated based on the system's current data: personal active volume, first line, deep volume, and activity period. If one of the parameters changes, the status may change under the program rules.

Status requires maintaining activity: personal active volume, first line, deep volume, and activity period.

DAO governance is a mechanism through which the community can take part in discussing and voting on important project matters.

Eligibility and voting weight are displayed in the Voting section of the Personal Dashboard under the governance rules active at that time.

Voting may concern project parameters, development stages, and certain system rules — if these matters are officially put to the DAO.

The idea of series of cycles with a managed restart through the DAO.

The current status of the DAO mechanics can be seen on the "Voting" page in your personal dashboard.

No. The correct wording: Atlas is not a full-fledged DAO, but uses DAO-inspired mechanics for certain community governance and voting functions.

No. Voting can only work within officially permitted topics. Security matters, smart contract operation, legal restrictions, and critical parameters may be outside the scope of voting.

Atlas cannot sign transactions for the participant or control the participant’s wallet. A confirmed Support Amount is handled by the applicable smart contract and liquidity mechanics defined by its code.

No. Private keys and seed phrases remain only with the wallet owner.

No. The seed phrase must never be shared with anyone.

The main risks are network errors, smart contract operation, human errors, choosing the wrong network, and the general limitations of Web3 infrastructure.

Don't connect your wallet, don't sign transactions, verify the official domain, and contact support.

Atlas should not be described as a classic investment with guaranteed income. It is a Web3 participation mechanic through a smart contract, where the user evaluates the rules, the calculation model, and the risks themselves.

Atlas may operate through a smart contract without a classic legal entity, but this does not remove the need for rules, risk notices, a data policy, disclaimers, and compliance with applicable requirements in different countries.

The user confirms the transaction in their own wallet and must verify the network, address, amount, and action. A blockchain transaction cannot be canceled after confirmation.

The official Atlas website and the documents published on it. Webinars, presentations, posts, translations, and partner materials are supplementary.

To help support assist you faster, send the wallet address, tx hash, network, a screenshot of the error, and a brief description of the problem right away.

Your seed phrase, private key, access codes, and full device data.

A tx hash is the public identifier of a transaction on the blockchain. With it, you can check the operation's status, addresses, amount, network, and error on BscScan: https://bscscan.com/ (https://bscscan.com/)

The network has not yet confirmed the transaction, or the gas was too low. Pending does not mean lost funds; wait for the final success/failed status.

There may be insufficient gas, the wrong network, an insufficient balance, or a contract condition error.

Switch your wallet to the correct BNB Smart Chain network and refresh the page.

Support can check the tx hash, wallet address, network, transaction status, MetaMask error, and how the action is displayed in the dashboard. Support cannot cancel a confirmed transaction or restore a seed phrase.

Response time depends on the team's workload and the complexity of the issue.

The webinar schedule is shown in your personal dashboard: language, topic, host, date, time, time zone, and a link to apply/join.

The first MetaMask connection.

Important

A Smart Cycle is not an investment instrument. The return of a Support Amount, Delta, Claim Assistance and Partner Rewards are not guaranteed and depend on smart-contract rules, participant activity, qualification conditions and available liquidity.

sources.content:
Use the official term

No matching term

Try a shorter query or choose a category above.

Atlas System

A digital mutual funding platform built on Web3, smart contracts and DAO-inspired mechanics.

Participant

A person whose Web3 wallet is connected to Atlas and who voluntarily uses the available functions.

Personal Dashboard

The participant interface for creating and tracking Smart Cycles, using Claim, viewing activity and accessing the Partner Program.

Atlas Community

Participants and contributors connected through the Atlas ecosystem.

Smart Contract

Code deployed on a blockchain that executes predefined rules without manual changes for an individual participant.

DAO-inspired mechanics

Transparent, rule-based and community-oriented mechanics. This wording does not mean that Atlas is currently a fully decentralised autonomous organisation.

Web3 Wallet

A blockchain wallet used to connect to Atlas and approve transactions.

MetaMask

A non-custodial Web3 wallet that can connect to Atlas and BNB Smart Chain.

BNB Smart Chain (BSC)

The blockchain network used by Smart Cycle 1.

BEP-20

The token standard used by assets such as USDT on BNB Smart Chain.

USDT

The settlement asset used by Smart Cycle 1 on BNB Smart Chain. Always verify the network and token contract.

Gas fee (BNB)

The blockchain network fee paid in BNB. It is separate from the Support Amount and Atlas Platform Fees.

Non-custodial wallet

A wallet whose access keys remain under the participant’s control. Atlas does not hold or recover those keys.

Wallet address

A public blockchain identifier. It is safe to verify publicly, but it must never be confused with a seed phrase or private key.

Transaction Hash (Tx Hash)

A unique identifier used to find and verify a blockchain transaction.

BscScan

An independent blockchain explorer used to inspect addresses, contracts and transactions on BNB Smart Chain.

Contract Address Registry

The official Knowledge Hub list of Atlas contract addresses and their purpose.

On-chain

Recorded on the blockchain and independently verifiable through a block explorer.

Smart Cycle

A smart-contract interaction in which a participant voluntarily provides a Support Amount under the selected cycle rules.

Smart Cycle 1

The first pilot financial product and current core of the Atlas ecosystem. It is not an investment instrument.

Support Amount

The USDT amount voluntarily provided when a Smart Cycle is created. Do not describe it as a deposit or investment.

Lockup Flow

A flow with a fixed term. When the term ends, the participant may use Claim Assistance under the smart-contract rules.

Daily Flow

A 200-day flow in which assistance may be claimed daily under the smart-contract rules; the original Support Amount is included in daily claims.

Cycle Term

The duration or claim schedule selected for a Smart Cycle.

Delta

The calculated additional assistance defined by the selected cycle rules. Delta is not guaranteed.

Claim Assistance (Claim)

The action that requests available assistance from the smart contract when its conditions are met. Availability depends on the rules, participant activity and liquidity.

Available Liquidity

Funds currently available under the relevant smart-contract and liquidity conditions.

Contract Test

The short Lockup Flow option intended for checking wallet connection and contract interaction with a small Support Amount.

Active

A cycle status showing that the selected cycle or claim period is still in progress.

Completed

A cycle status showing that the selected term has ended or the cycle has finished under the contract rules.

Partner Program

The Atlas Level Compression model through which eligible participants may receive Partner Rewards from Delta under current rules.

Referral Link

A personal link that connects a newly invited participant to a referrer.

Partner Status

The participant’s current qualification level in the Partner Program.

Partner Structure

Participants connected through referral relationships below a participant.

Personal Active Cycle Volume

The participant’s own active Smart Cycle volume used for status qualification.

First-Line Active Cycle Volume

Active qualifying volume created by personally invited participants.

Partner Structure Active Cycle Volume

Active qualifying volume across the Partner Structure under the applicable rules.

Actual Partner Structure Volume

The structure volume before line-weighting coefficients are applied.

Weighted Partner Structure Volume

The structure volume after the current line-weighting coefficients are applied.

Qualifying Volume

The volume counted toward Partner Status requirements after applicable flow and structure coefficients.

Compression

A rule that passes the applicable percentage difference through levels according to Partner Status.

Partner Reward

A reward calculated from Delta generated within the Partner Structure, subject to current status and compression rules.

Matching Reward

A status-dependent reward calculated from Partner Rewards of personally invited participants when qualification conditions are met.

Incoming Flow

All USDT received by the relevant Smart Contract for the selected period.

Outgoing Flow

All USDT sent from the relevant Smart Contract for the selected period.

Cycle Claims

Outgoing assistance claimed through Smart Cycles, including applicable Delta.

Platform Fees

Atlas fees charged according to the current product rules. Blockchain gas fees are separate.

Current Atlas System Liquidity

The current USDT held by the relevant Smart Contract or Atlas liquidity position as labelled on the official page. It is not the total liquidity of an external pool.

LP Position

Atlas liquidity-provider assets held in an external decentralised liquidity pool.

External Claim Liquidity

Liquidity available through an external pool for claim-related operations, subject to current contract mechanics.

Governance

The set of mechanisms through which eligible participants may take part in defined Atlas decisions.

Voting Balance

The voting weight displayed in the Personal Dashboard under the rules currently active in the interface.

Vote

A recorded choice on an available governance proposal. Always check the current interface for eligibility and weight.

Smart Cycle 2

A possible future protocol stage. Its launch date and final mechanics have not been approved; Smart Cycle 1 remains the current focus.

Language matters

Atlas Smart Cycles are not investment instruments. Delta, Claim Assistance and Partner Rewards are not guaranteed and depend on the smart-contract rules, participant activity, qualification conditions and available liquidity.

The mechanism in four steps

Connect a compatible Web3 wallet. No email or phone registration is required.

Choose Lockup Flow or Daily Flow, set the Support Amount in USDT and confirm it in the wallet.

The contract fixes the selected term and Delta calculation and records the operation on-chain.

When the conditions are met, request assistance and verify the transaction on BscScan.

Who does what

Component

Role

Atlas personal account

Displays cycles, calculations, Claim availability, operation history and system indicators.

Web3 wallet

Identifies the participant and authorizes blockchain transactions.

Smart Cycle contract

Receives support and executes operations according to encoded rules.

BNB Smart Chain

Records transactions and provides the blockchain infrastructure.

BscScan

Allows anyone to independently verify wallet and contract transactions.

Where assistance comes from

Incoming participant support forms the liquidity available inside the smart contract. The contract redistributes funds according to its code; funds are not sent to external trading platforms, lending services or third-party investment pools.

A displayed or calculated amount is therefore not the same as a guaranteed payment. Claim execution depends on the applicable rules and sufficient contract liquidity at the time of the request.

What is automatic — and what you control

Automated by the system

Controlled by the participant

Applies the selected cycle conditions.

Decides whether to participate and how much support to provide.

Fixes the term and applicable Delta calculation at creation.

Chooses Lockup Flow or Daily Flow and the applicable cycle.

Records operations on BNB Smart Chain and displays their status.

Reviews and confirms every support and Claim transaction.

Reads current contract data.

Checks the official site, network, amount and contract details.

Automation does not create a payment guarantee and cannot replace the participant’s transaction confirmation.

Lockup Flow and Daily Flow

The cycle lasts from 10 minutes to 30 days. Assistance can be requested after the selected term ends.

The cycle lasts 200 days. Assistance can be requested daily under the contract terms; the original Support Amount is included in the daily assistance calculation.

Tariffs, plan limits and step-by-step Claim actions are covered in the separate Smart Cycle instruction.

What you see in the personal account

The personal account is the working interface for the smart contract. It shows active and completed cycles, Support Amounts, calculated Delta, Claim availability, operation history and current System Health indicators.

Transparency by design

Every smart-contract operation is recorded on BNB Smart Chain. Participants can review their cycles in the personal account and independently check wallet and contract transactions on BscScan. Distribution rules are fixed in code and cannot be manually changed for an individual participant.

Open this transaction ↗

Official contract addresses, audits and verification instructions are collected in the Contracts & BscScan and Audits sections of the Knowledge Hub.

Limits and risks

Creating a Smart Cycle does not guarantee the return of the Support Amount.

A calculated Delta does not guarantee that the amount will be available to Claim.

Claim execution depends on the contract rules and available liquidity.

Atlas System does not describe Smart Cycle as a deposit, bank account or conventional investment product.

Confirmed blockchain transactions normally cannot be reversed.

Participation is voluntary. Before every transaction, check the official website, wallet network, contract details and amount shown in the wallet.

BNB Chain in Plain English: USDT BEP-20, Fees, and Transaction Confirmation
sources.content:
Disclaimer: This article is for educational purposes only. It is not financial, legal, or investment advice.

“Send USDT,” “choose BEP-20,” and “keep BNB for the fee” may sound like three details of the same thing. In fact, they refer to different layers:

USDT is a token name and ticker.

BNB Smart Chain (BSC) is the blockchain network processing the operation.

BEP-20 is a common fungible-token standard on that network.

BNB is BSC’s native asset and is normally used to pay network gas.

Understanding the distinction helps prevent one of the most common mistakes: sending a token over a network that the receiving wallet or service does not support.

Key takeaways

BNB Chain is an ecosystem; BNB Smart Chain is its EVM-compatible smart-contract network.

BEP-20 is a token standard, not a coin or a recipient address.

Sending a BEP-20 token normally requires a small BNB balance for gas.

The labels “USDT” and “BEP-20” are not enough: verify the network and token-contract address.

A Success status proves execution, not that the user chose the intended address, token, or action.

BNB Chain and BNB Smart Chain

BNB Chain is the broader ecosystem. BNB Smart Chain, commonly called BSC, is its EVM-compatible network for smart contracts and decentralized applications.

EVM compatibility means that BSC uses an account and contract model familiar from Ethereum. Addresses usually begin with 0x, and many Web3 wallets can connect to the network.

Matching address formats do not make networks interchangeable. The same-looking 0x address can exist on BSC, Ethereum, and other EVM networks, while balances and histories remain separate in each network.

What BEP-20 means

BEP-20 is a technical standard for tokens on BSC. It defines a shared interface for actions such as checking a balance, transferring tokens, and granting a spending allowance.

Think of the network as a railway, the token standard as the track gauge, and a particular token as a train. The letters “USDT” on the train do not by themselves tell you which network it is on or which contract created it.

In exchange and wallet interfaces, “USDT BEP-20” usually means a USDT-labelled token transferred through BNB Smart Chain. Yet a ticker is not unique: anyone can technically create a token called USDT. The reliable identifier is the token-contract address on the specific network.

Tether’s official supported-protocol page and listed contract addresses can change. Users should consult the current official source for the relevant asset and compare it with the address used by the sending and receiving services. A USDT contract address from Ethereum, Tron, or another network must not be assumed to identify a BSC token.

Why the fee is paid in BNB

The network charges for computation and block space. This charge is called gas, and BNB is the native asset used for gas on BSC.

A wallet may therefore show 100 USDT but still be unable to send it when its BNB balance is zero. The USDT is present, but calling the token contract’s transfer function requires a separate network transaction.

The fee depends on:

the amount of gas the operation consumes;

the current gas price;

the complexity of the action.

A simple token transfer and a complex smart-contract interaction may cost different amounts. Wallets display an estimate before signing. A fixed “permanent” fee should not be hard-coded into instructions because network parameters and conditions change.

The recipient does not need to pay gas merely to see an incoming token. They will need BNB when they later send that token or perform another BSC transaction.

What happens after you press Send

The wallet prepares a call to the token contract.

The user reviews the network, recipient, amount, and estimated fee.

The wallet signs the transaction with the user’s key.

The transaction is broadcast and receives a unique hash.

A validator includes it in a block.

The network confirms the state and the block reaches finality under BSC rules.

BNB Chain documentation describes Fast Finality when enough validators provide finality votes. Exact timing depends on current network behavior, and a centralized platform may impose its own confirmation threshold before crediting a deposit.

Useful status distinctions include:

Pending: the transaction is still awaiting inclusion or processing.

Success: execution completed successfully.

Failed: execution did not complete, although some BNB may still have been spent on computation.

Credited by a service: an exchange or platform has applied its own deposit rules after on-chain confirmation.

What Success actually proves

A Success status in a block explorer means that the network executed the submitted transaction successfully.

It does not prove that:

the user selected the intended recipient;

the recipient supports the network;

the token is authentic rather than a copy with the same ticker;

the action matched the user’s intention;

a centralized service has already credited the deposit.

The blockchain validates the signature and execution rules. It cannot know which address the user intended to paste.

A practical example

Alice wants to send Bob 50 USDT through BNB Smart Chain.

Before sending:

Bob obtains a deposit address specifically for BNB Smart Chain from his wallet or service.

Alice selects BNB Smart Chain / BEP-20 as the withdrawal network.

They verify the token-contract address, not only the USDT label.

Alice keeps enough BNB for gas.

She sends a small test amount first.

After Success, they inspect the token-transfer section on BscScan and confirm the token, amount, and recipient.

If Bob uses an exchange, they wait for its required confirmations.

A test transfer does not remove every risk and incurs its own fee, but it can reveal an incorrect address or network before a larger transfer.

How to verify a transfer

Save the transaction hash, a string beginning with 0x. Open the official BscScan explorer and paste the hash into search.

Check:

Status: Success or Failed;

From: the sender address;

Interacted With / To: the token-contract address;

Tokens Transferred: token, amount, sender, and recipient;

Transaction Fee: the actual BNB fee;

the block number and time;

confirmation or finality information, where displayed.

Do not confuse the top-level To field with the final token recipient. In a BEP-20 transfer, the transaction is sent to the token contract; the recipient address is passed inside the contract call. The Tokens Transferred section is generally the clearer view.

Five common mistakes

1. The networks do not match

The recipient expects an Ethereum deposit, but the sender chooses BSC. The address format may match while the service fails to credit the deposit.

2. The recipient address is wrong

Clipboard malware can replace copied addresses. Compare the beginning and end, and for significant transfers verify the full address or a QR code through a trusted channel.

3. The ticker is checked, but the contract is not

Multiple tokens can use the same name and symbol. Verify the contract address through a current official source.

4. There is no BNB for gas

The wallet holds USDT but cannot send it. Keep a modest BNB gas reserve rather than relying on a fixed amount from an old guide.

5. The receiving service does not support BEP-20 deposits

Tokens may exist on the address on-chain while the exchange’s internal system does not recognize them. Check supported deposit networks before sending.

Pre-signing checklist

BNB Smart Chain is selected, not opBNB, Ethereum, or another network.

The recipient address comes directly from its owner or the receiving service.

The withdrawal and deposit networks match.

The token-contract address is verified through an up-to-date official source.

The wallet has enough BNB for gas.

The amount and fee are understood.

A first-time route is tested with a small amount.

The transaction hash is saved.

No seed phrase or private key was disclosed; neither is needed to verify a transaction.

Conclusion

“USDT BEP-20” describes more than an asset name: it combines a token contract with the BNB Smart Chain network. BNB pays for execution, and the outcome can be independently checked using the transaction hash.

The central rule is simple: before signing, match the network on both sides and verify both the token contract and recipient address. A Success status confirms what the network received; it does not correct a user’s mistaken choice.

Sources and Further Reading

BNB Chain Docs: Tokens not showing in wallet

BNB Chain Docs: BSC wallet configuration

BNB Chain Docs: BEP-20 reference in benchmark design

Binance Academy: BEP-20

sources.title: How to Check a Transaction and Contract Balance on BscScan
sources.content:
A blockchain record can be checked independently. If a transaction was submitted to BNB Smart Chain, you can look it up on BscScan by its transaction hash. You can also inspect the assets held at a smart contract address.

The key is to read the data correctly. A Success status means that the network executed the transaction without reverting it. It does not prove that the address belongs to the intended project, that a token is genuine, or that the transaction is safe or beneficial.

This article is for educational purposes only. It is not financial advice and does not guarantee the safety of any project, contract, or transaction.

What you need

Prepare one of these identifiers:

a transaction hash (or TxHash), which identifies one transaction;

a wallet or contract address, which identifies an account or smart contract.

Both usually begin with 0x, but they are not interchangeable. Obtain contract addresses from an official project source and compare the full string. A name or ticker is not enough: unrelated tokens may use the same name.

You do not need to connect a wallet to view public BscScan data. Never enter a seed phrase or private key—BscScan does not need either.

Step 1: Find the transaction

Open bscscan.com.

Paste the complete transaction hash into the search bar.

Open the Transaction Details result.

If no result appears, check that:

the transaction was sent on BNB Smart Chain, not another network;

the hash was copied in full;

the wallet actually broadcast the transaction;

the explorer has had time to index a newly submitted transaction.

Step 2: Read the transaction fields

Check these fields in order:

StatusSuccess means execution completed without a revert. Pending means the transaction has not yet been included. Failed means execution reverted. A failed contract call normally does not complete its intended state changes, but gas used may still be charged.

Block and confirmationsThe block number identifies where the transaction was included. Confirmations count the blocks added afterwards. Services may require different confirmation counts. BNB Smart Chain has a fast-finality mechanism and a probabilistic fallback in which additional blocks increase confidence.

TimestampConfirm the date and time. BscScan can display UTC, so account for your time zone.

FromThis is the address that initiated the transaction. Compare it with the expected sender.

To / Interacted WithFor a simple transfer, this is the recipient. For a contract call, it is the contract directly called by the transaction. Compare the complete address with the project’s officially published address.

ValueThis is the native BNB sent at the top level. A BEP-20 transfer may show 0 BNB here because the token movement is displayed separately.

BEP-20 Tokens TransferredThis section shows token transfer events, including token, sender, recipient, and amount. Verify the token contract address, not just its name, icon, or ticker.

Transaction FeeThis is the BNB paid for execution. It is not the transferred amount.

Transaction Action and Input DataWhen the contract interface is known, BscScan may decode the function and its parameters. Treat the human-readable summary as a useful aid and still verify addresses, amounts, and emitted events.

For complex calls, also inspect:

Internal Txns, which shows internal calls and BNB movements involving contracts;

Logs, which shows events emitted during execution.

Example: reading a 100 USDT transfer

Suppose a user intends to send 100 USDT to a contract. A basic check should confirm that:

Status is Success;

From matches the user’s address;

Interacted With matches the intended contract;

BEP-20 Tokens Transferred shows 100 units moving from the user to the intended address;

the USDT token contract address matches the official USDT address for BNB Smart Chain;

Value may be 0 BNB, while the gas fee is paid in BNB.

No single matching field is sufficient. A call to an impersonating contract can also have a Success status.

Step 3: Check a contract balance

Paste the official contract address into BscScan.

Confirm the full address on the result page.

Read BNB Balance for native BNB held at the address.

Open Token Holdings to inspect BEP-20 assets.

Locate a specific token by its contract address and check the amount.

“Contract balance” is not one universal number:

BNB and USDT balances are separate;

an address can hold many tokens, including unsolicited spam tokens;

a system may use several contract or treasury addresses;

assets may later move to another address;

a current balance does not reveal all liabilities or who has the economic claim to the assets.

For a more direct BEP-20 check, open the exact token contract, select Contract → Read Contract, find balanceOf, and enter the address being checked. This is a read-only query and requires no transaction or gas. The result may use the token’s smallest unit; apply the token’s decimals value to convert it to the displayed amount.

What “Verified” means

On BscScan, contract source verification has different levels:

Exact Match means the published source and constructor parameters were matched to the deployed bytecode;

Similar Match means the bytecode matches an existing verified contract, but constructor arguments are not included in that match;

Unverified means no matching source is published and only bytecode is available.

Verification makes code easier to inspect. It is not a security audit and does not prove that the code has no vulnerabilities.

If the address is a proxy, its active logic may live in a separate implementation contract and may be changeable by an authorized upgrader. Check whether BscScan identifies a proxy, follow the implementation address, and determine who controls upgrades. Reviewing only the proxy shell gives an incomplete picture.

What BscScan can—and cannot—establish

BscScan can help establish that:

a transaction was included in a block;

one address called another;

contracts emitted particular logs;

an address currently has a particular BNB or token balance;

published source was matched to bytecode at the stated verification level.

It does not by itself establish:

who owns or controls an address;

that a token is genuine based on its name;

that administrators lack dangerous powers;

that code is free of vulnerabilities;

that liquidity exists;

that a frontend will remain available;

that funds will be returned or generate a yield.

Final checklist

I found the hash on BNB Smart Chain.

I compared the complete From and To / Interacted With addresses.

I verified the token contract address.

I distinguished native Value, BEP-20 movement, and gas fee.

I reviewed Internal Txns and Logs where relevant.

I checked BNB and each required token separately.

For a proxy, I checked the implementation and upgrade authority.

My conclusion relies on several fields, not only Success.

Sources and Further Reading

sources.title: DAO Mechanics: How a Community Can Participate in a Digital Platform’s Development
sources.content:
DAO stands for “decentralized autonomous organization.” The name can suggest a system that operates entirely on its own, without administrators, teams, or other human decision-makers. In practice, a DAO is a set of rules and tools through which participants can propose, discuss, vote on, and oversee decisions.

Projects differ greatly in their degree of decentralization. Instead of asking only “Is this a DAO?”, ask who can propose decisions, who can vote, how voting power is calculated, who executes the result, and whether that execution can be verified.

The usual stages of DAO governance

1. Proposal

A participant or working group defines a proposed action. A well-formed proposal explains the problem, the desired outcome, costs, risks, implementation period, and success criteria.

Without clear proposal standards, voting can become a non-binding opinion poll.

2. Discussion

Before a vote, the community examines the reasoning, asks questions, and suggests changes. Discussion may take place on a forum or another public platform.

This stage is as important as the vote itself. Participants need evidence and alternatives, not merely “For” and “Against” buttons.

3. Voting

The governance rules should answer several questions in advance:

Who is eligible to vote?

How is voting power calculated?

Is there a quorum?

What majority is required?

How long does voting remain open?

Can voting power be delegated?

How are conflicts of interest and concentrated influence addressed?

One system may assign one vote to each participant. Another may use tokens, contribution, reputation, or a combination of factors. Every model involves trade-offs. Capital-weighted voting makes mass creation of empty accounts less useful, but gives large holders more influence. Equal voting requires a reliable way to distinguish one person from many wallets controlled by that person.

4. Execution

An approved decision may be executed automatically by a smart contract or manually by an authorized team or multisignature wallet.

Automatic execution reduces the possibility of an arbitrary refusal to act, but increases the cost of mistakes in the proposal or code. Manual execution allows a final safety check but requires trust in the executors.

5. Accountability

After implementation, participants should be able to see what changed. For an on-chain action, this may be a transaction or updated contract state. For an off-chain decision, the community needs a report, an accountable owner, and measurable results.

What a DAO may decide

DAO mechanisms are commonly used for:

product-development priorities;

grants and budget allocations;

selection of service providers or auditors;

changes to parameters designed to be adjustable;

creation of working groups;

community rules;

selection of a future protocol version.

However, a vote cannot rewrite the past in an immutable contract. If a live contract does not allow a parameter to be changed, a community decision cannot alter it retroactively. A new contract and a user migration may be required.

A DAO is not risk-free

Users should examine:

voting concentration: can one participant or a small group determine the outcome?

low turnout: does a result represent the community or only a few active wallets?

information quality: do voters have enough evidence to decide?

enforceability: who implements the decision and by what deadline?

administrative powers: which keys and roles remain controlled by a team?

governance attacks: can voting power be bought, borrowed, or temporarily accumulated?

legal status: governance mechanics do not override applicable law.

On-chain voting makes actions observable. It does not automatically make a voting model fair or ensure that participants made a well-informed decision.

What is confirmed about Atlas System

Atlas System’s main website describes Governance as a platform through which the community will be able to propose changes, discuss ideas, and help shape the ecosystem’s future architecture.

The same website’s roadmap places the decentralized Governance platform in Q4 2026. At the time of writing, it should therefore be treated as a planned product, not represented as an already available feature.

Public Atlas materials also describe a broader concept: when activity in a protocol is exhausted, the community may be presented with options for the next protocol, supported by economic models, and a winning option may be recorded on-chain. However, the public pages do not provide enough final detail on voter eligibility, voting weights, quorum, delegation, or execution to describe the finished Governance design as established.

There is also an important distinction between Governance and a live Smart Cycle. Terms recorded for an existing Smart Cycle are not changed retroactively by a community vote. Governance may influence future decisions and protocol versions only within the powers that are technically and organizationally provided.

Atlas’s technical registry describes parts of the current infrastructure and its LP position as managed through a SAFE with a 2-of-3 signature threshold at the registry snapshot. That is a multisignature control mechanism, not public DAO voting. The two governance layers should not be confused.

What to check when Atlas Governance launches

Users should look for clear answers to seven questions:

Who may submit a proposal, and is a deposit required?

Who may vote, and how is voting power calculated?

What quorum and majority are required?

Where are discussions and supporting evidence published?

Are votes and final results recorded on-chain?

Who executes a decision, and is there a time delay?

Which parts of live contracts can actually be changed?

Until those rules are published and the platform is live, it is accurate to describe the direction of Atlas Governance, but not to assign it specific operational capabilities.

The key takeaway

A DAO is not a magical replacement for management. It is a way to formalize and verify community participation. Effective DAO governance combines a clear proposal, open discussion, transparent voting, controlled execution, and accountability.

For users, the label matters less than the distribution of real authority. Examine who controls code, funds, and execution today—and evaluate planned future capabilities separately.

This article is for educational purposes. A roadmap is not a guarantee of a launch date or final feature set.
